Therefore they left nothing undone, with the greatest diligence, to prevent the synod from meeting at the appointed time.

units.la: feclis suis, qui sibi à synodo metuebant, agunt, ut contra synodum futuram, licet regia authoritate solenniter indictam, protestarentur, tanquam illegitimam, utpote quod in Classibus ad deputatorum electionem admissa fuerint seniorum (quos tertio quoque verbo per contumeliam Laicos vocabant) suffragia, iisque par potestas cum verbi pastoribus concederetur: Multa alia hujus generis subterfugia indies producebant: Et cum subdolæ istæ molitiones ex animi sui sententia non succederent, ad alia astuta consilia se conferunt.
units.tr: With their supporters and adherents, who feared the synod for their own sake, they acted so that they might protest against the coming synod, though solemnly convened by royal authority, as illegitimate. Their reason was that the votes of the elders (whom every third word they insultingly called laymen) had been admitted in the classes to the election of the delegates, and that equal power had been granted to them with the ministers of the Word. They produced many other evasions of this kind day by day. And when these deceitful schemes did not succeed as they wished, they turned to other crafty plans.

units.la: Etenim vulgo cognitum fuit, vias in tractu Glasguensi à latronibus obsessas esse; ita ut, qui Glasguam ad synodum adventuri essent, cogerentur arma secum ferre defensiva, quibus à prædonum ibidem grassantium impetu se tuerentur; cum vero temporibus pacatis per leges illud non liceret, cum deputato regio agunt, eique tandem persuadent Episcopi, ut ad synodum delegatos sine armis, atque numerosiore comitatu clientelæ & familiarium Glasguam adesse juberet, aliisque omnibus ad synodum non deputatis severe interdiceret, ne Glasguam accederent: hac arte persuasum fuit Episcopis, aut nullos habituros se accusatores, aut oblatam occasionem declinandi Synodum, utpote ad quam non esset sibi tutus accessus, in urbe scilicet adversariorum etiam armatorum plena: Sed prudentia fœderatorum omnes illæ veršutiæ frustra fuerunt, frequentiorique comitatu licet stipati, ac armis defensivis muniti Glasguam advenientes, nihil aliud sibi propositum fuisse ostenderunt, quam ut se contra subitariam vim tuerentur, si quæ imminerent aut à latronibus in via, aut à vicinia, quæ eorum clientelis referta fuit, quibus, temporibus hisce dubiis sese securé committere vix tutum judicabant.
units.tr: Indeed, it was commonly known that the roads in the Glasgow district were beset by robbers. So those who were to come to the synod at Glasgow were forced to carry defensive arms, to protect themselves against the attacks of the brigands raging there. But since, in peaceful times, the law did not permit this, the bishops dealt with the royal deputy and at last persuaded him to order that the delegates to the synod come to Glasgow without arms and with a larger retinue of clients and servants. He was also to forbid severely all others not delegated to the synod from coming to Glasgow. By this trick the bishops were persuaded either that they would have no accusers, or that they had an opportunity to avoid the synod, since it would not be safe for them to approach it, in a city full of their armed enemies. But the prudence of the Covenanters made all these tricks vain. Arriving at Glasgow with a larger retinue, and protected with defensive arms, they showed that their only purpose was to defend themselves against any sudden violence that might threaten them, either from robbers on the road or from the neighbourhood, which was full of the bishops' clients. In these doubtful times they judged it scarcely safe to trust themselves securely to such people.

units.la: Cum vero accepissent Illustrissimum Marchionem Hamiltonium... Hammiltonium[?], summum regis Sereniss. deputatum, 16 Novembris Glasguam adventurum, nobiles omnes obviam ei procedunt, ac frequenti D. Senatorum regiorum ac clientum comitatu stipatum ad hospitium deducunt.
units.tr: When they learned that the most illustrious Marquis of Hamilton, the highest deputy of the most serene king, would come to Glasgow on 16 November, all the noblemen went out to meet him. With a large train of the king's lords and clients around him, they escorted him to his lodging.

units.la: Varii interim habebantur congressus praeparatorii, ac ex edicti praescripto 21. Novembris aperitur synodus, praesente Deputato regio; Post septem dierum in synodo moram, tandem de synodo discesserat, ac, nomine regis, synodi dissolutionem severe imperaverat; & scriptum declinatorium ab Episcopis compositum offerri jubet per procuratorem, quo synodum totam conquisitis undique rationibus aut rationum praetextibus recusaverant, & alios judices magis competentes appellaverant: Sed tam interdictio quam appellatio frustra fuerunt. Nam folenni protestatione ad mandatum dissolutionis respondet synodus; & scriptum illud Episcoporum declinatorium excutitur, ac ad singula objecta fuse respondetur: Cum vero Deputati regii reditum frustra exspectandum esse cernerent synodi membra, ad actiones ventum est; quarum quaedam capita tantum & indicem subjiciam: Inquiritur de ἀνυφτμία[?] registrorum synodalium, & authentica esse declarantur: Damnantur conventus quidam Ecclesiastici, qui synodorum nationalium nomine veniebant, eorumque ad oculum ostenditur nullitas: Omnium Episcoporum causae sigillatim examinantur; ac decernitur omnes esse ab Episcopali functione removendos & ex quatuordecim quos numerabat Scotia episcopos, octo excommunicantur, quatuor ab omni ecclesiastica functione excluduntur, duobus indultum ut pastoris munere defungi possent; & Censura in complures pastores fertur: Damnatur Dioecesanus Episcopatus; quinque articuli Perthenses; libri liturgiae, canonum, ordinationis, rejicitur Celsa Commissio, & quicquid in Ecclesiam irrepsit post annum 1580; quando primum fœdus illud nationale sancitum fuerat; ejus genuinum sensum de articulis controversis expromunt; ac postliminio in usum revocant constitutiones ecclesiasticas in prima & puriori reformatione latas, quibus diu floruit disciplinæ vigor, doctrinæ puritas, cultus divini simplicitas, & pastorum unitas: Cui volupe erit, omnia specialius designata cognoscere, consulat fusiorem & pleniorem Synodi descriptionem subjunctam, ubi non solum fundamenta quibus conclusiones & decreta Synodica innituntur, verumetiam scriptorum illorum publicorum, de quibus facta mentio, medullam invenient: hoc est; Episcoporum protestationem contra Synodum; Deputati regii edictum de dissolvenda synodo, & Synodi ad utrumque scriptum, singulaque eorundem capita responsiones, uti etiam literas à Synodo ad serenissimum regem exaratas, & de verbo in verbum translatas: quæ imprimis consulendæ sunt.
units.tr: Meanwhile various preparatory meetings were held, and on 21 November, as the edict prescribed, the synod was opened in the presence of the royal deputy. After he had spent seven days in the synod, he at last departed from it. In the king's name he severely ordered the synod dissolved, and commanded that a declinatory writing drawn up by the bishops be presented through their proctor. In it they had rejected the whole synod, using every reason or pretext of reasons they could gather, and had appealed to other, more competent judges. But both the prohibition and the appeal were in vain. For the synod answered the order of dissolution with a solemn protest, and that declinatory writing of the bishops was examined, and each of its objections was answered at length. But when the members of the synod saw that the return of the royal deputies was vainly to be awaited, they proceeded to the actions. I will set out only some heads of these and an index. The synodal registers were inquired into and declared authentic. Certain ecclesiastical gatherings, which claimed to be national synods, were condemned, and their nullity was made plain to the eye. The causes of all the bishops were examined one by one, and it was decreed that all were to be removed from the episcopal office. Of the fourteen bishops that Scotland then numbered, eight were excommunicated, four were excluded from every ecclesiastical function, and to two was granted that they might still perform the duties of a minister. Censure was also passed on several ministers. The Diocesan episcopacy was condemned; the five Perth articles; the books of liturgy, canons and ordination were rejected; the High Commission was rejected, and whatever had crept into the Church after the year 1580, when that first national covenant was ratified. They set out the genuine sense of the covenant concerning the disputed articles, and by right of return they restored to use the ecclesiastical constitutions enacted in the first and purer Reformation, under which the vigour of discipline, the purity of doctrine, the simplicity of divine worship and the unity of the ministers had long flourished. Whoever is pleased to know all things designated more particularly, let him consult the fuller and more complete description of the synod appended below. There he will find not only the foundations on which the synodal conclusions and decrees rest, but also the very marrow of those public writings that have been mentioned: namely, the bishops' protest against the synod; the royal deputy's edict dissolving the synod; and the synod's replies to each of these writings and to their individual heads. Also included are the letter written by the synod to the most serene king, translated word for word. These are above all to be consulted.

units.la: Plena narratio Synodi Glasguensis.
units.tr: Full account of the Synod of Glasgow.

units.la: Post ultro citroque varios habitos congressus: Inchoata tandem fuit nationalis Synodus Glasguæ, 21. Novemb. anni 1638. Regii deputati mandato (cum sui muneris esse diceret, absente prioris synodi præside, eum nominare qui precibus ac solenni concione actionem hanc sacram auspicaretur) Reverendo seni, Iohanni Belo, seniori urbis pastori, provincia aperiendi synodum demandabatur, & ille, precibus ad Deum fusis, ut servis suis in Christi nomine congregatis spiritu veritatis & pacis adesse ac præesse dignaretur; ac insigni & appositá concione, qua omnes officii sui serio admonebat, Synodi hujus tot piorum votis desideratæ Aperturam fecit: Cujus sermonem excepit Deputatus regius, literasque fidei & mandati à rege serenissimo datas, Thomæ Sandilandio, (quem pater Iacobus Sandilandius anterioris Synodi Scriba vicarium jam delegit) publice legendas tradit; quibus plenam Marchioni Hammiltonio potestatem tradit Indicendi Synodos Nationales in regno Scotiæ,ubi & quando ipsi visum fuerit,ibidemq; se ipsum tanquam nostrum Commissarium gerendi,omniaque eisdem tenendis inservientia se-cundum leges & praxin Ecclesiæ & regni Scotiæ, præstandi.
units.tr: After various meetings had been held on both sides, the national Synod was at last begun at Glasgow on 21 November 1638. The royal commissioner, saying that it was his duty, since the president of the previous synod was absent, to name someone to open this sacred business with prayer and a solemn sermon, assigned the task of opening the synod to the reverend old man John Bell, senior minister of the city. He poured out prayers to God that He would deign to be present and preside over his servants gathered in the name of Christ, with the spirit of truth and peace. Then, with a remarkable and fitting sermon in which he solemnly reminded all of their duty, he opened this synod, which had been so much desired by the prayers of so many godly people. After his sermon, the royal commissioner took up the letters of authority and commission given by the most serene king, and handed them to Thomas Sandilands (whom Father James Sandilands, scribe of the earlier synod, had already appointed as his deputy) to be read publicly. By these letters the king gave the Marquis Hamilton full power to call national synods in the kingdom of Scotland, where and when it should seem good to him, and there to act as our commissioner, and to perform all things serving to the holding of them, according to the laws and practice of the Church and kingdom of Scotland.

units.la: Eadem sessione delegati Classium seu presbyteriorum, urbium, & Academiarum, literas fiduciarias exhibent, quarum examinatio in subsequentes sessiones dilata fuit.
units.tr: In the same session, the delegates of the classes, or presbyteries, of the cities and universities presented their letters of credentials; their examination was postponed to later sessions.

units.la: ( 22. Novemb. sessione 2. )
units.tr: (22 November, second session.)

units.la: Præses pro tempore qui hanc actionem auspicatus fuit; significabat consultum esse, ut Præses, quem Scoti Moderatorem vocant, eligeretur, qui dirigendis Synodi actionibus præesset: Sed serenissimi Regis epistolam ad Synodum prælegi jussit deputatus regius, qua omnibus in Synodo mandat, eam reverentiam & obedientiam ut præstent Delegato Marchioni, quæ sibi præsenti à subditis debetur, quicquid porro regio nomine pollicebitur Marchio, id seratum[?] habiturum spondet, in cujus rei perpetuam memoriam præsentes has literas, publico synodi registro inserendas jubet. Quo concesso, rursus urgebatur Moderatoris electio, sine quo nihil operæpretii peragi potuit. Magna hic orta fuit disputatio, Deputato regio urgente, ut prius scriptum quoddam Episcoporum nomine sibi oblatum prælegeretur, dein ut deputatorum literæ fiduciariæ examinarentur, quibus peractis paratum se profitebatur ad novi Moderatoris electionem promovendam. Respondebant Synodici, neutrum adhuc concedi posse, non ultimum, nam quis futurus erit Iudex si difficultas aliqua in examinatione literarum fidei oboriatur ? Non posse Synodum, quæ Synodi nomine non veniat ante legitimam Præsidis & Scribæ electionem, qui fori hujus membra sint necessaria: Multo minus primum ob eandem rationem concedi potest, præsertim cum scriptum illud Episcoporum, ad Synodum sit destinatum, ibique prælegendum, quod vel cæcis conspicuum est, fieri non posse, quin prius synodi ipsius membra constituantur: quibus constitutis, utrumque se facturos spondent synodici. At contra utrumque tanquam injustum protestatur Deputatus regius: Consensit tamen tandem in Præsidis electionem, protestatione prius præmissa, Electione hac nihil derogatum iuri prærogativæ regiæ, legibus & consuetudinibus receptis, nec dignitati & authoritati Episcoporum, quibus Moderationis honor competit. Respondent Synodici; Sibi nunquam statutum jus regium aut legum vim diminuere; Quod vero ad Episcopos illos attinet, habendos pro reis quoad de ipsorum innocentia constiterit; Addebant alii vel eo nomine reos esse, quod prærogativa præsidentiæ per fas & nefas sibi arripuerint. Tandem ad Præsidis electionem ventum est, potioreque suffragiorum numero eligitur Alexander Hendersonus, pastor Ecclesiæ Leucherensis in Classe Andreapolitana: Deputatus interim in suffragio ferendo ita se gerebat, quasi electionem permitteret, ad eamque conniveret potius quam directe ratam haberet. Provinciam eleganti oratione ac ardentibus precibus capessit novus Præses.
units.tr: The president for the time, who had opened this business, stated that it was advisable to elect a president, whom the Scots call Moderator, to direct the proceedings of the synod. But the royal commissioner ordered the letter of the most serene king to the synod to be read out, in which he commands everyone in the synod to show that reverence and obedience which is owed by subjects to his delegate, the Marquis, in his presence; whatever the Marquis shall promise in the king's name, he pledges that the king will hold ratified; and in perpetual memory of this matter he orders these present letters to be entered in the public register of the synod. When this was granted, the election of a Moderator was pressed again, since nothing of worth could be done without one. A great dispute arose here, the royal commissioner insisting that first a certain writing presented to him in the name of the bishops should be read, and then that the letters of credentials of the commissioners should be examined; once these were done, he professed that he was ready to proceed to the election of a new Moderator. The members of the synod replied that neither demand could yet be granted, not least the last: for who would be the judge if some difficulty arose in examining the letters of credentials? The synod, which does not exist in the name of the synod before the lawful election of a president and a clerk, who are necessary members of this court, could not do so; much less could the first demand be granted for the same reason, especially since that writing of the bishops was addressed to the synod and was to be read there. That this cannot be done before the members of the synod itself are constituted is plain even to the blind; once they are constituted, the members of the synod promised that they would do both. On the contrary, the royal commissioner protested that both demands were unjust. Yet at last he consented to the election of a president, first making a protest that this election did no harm to the right of the royal prerogative, to the established laws and customs, or to the dignity and authority of the bishops, to whom the honour of moderating belongs. The members replied that they had never intended to diminish the royal right or the force of the laws; as for those bishops, they should be regarded as guilty only if their innocence were proved not to be established. Others added that they were guilty on this very ground, that they had seized for themselves the prerogative of presidency by right and wrong alike. At last they came to the election of a president, and by the greater number of votes Alexander Henderson, minister of the church of Leuchars in the St Andrews presbytery, was chosen. Meanwhile the commissioner, in giving his vote, so conducted himself as if he were allowing the election and conniving at it rather than directly approving it. The new president undertook the office with an elegant speech and fervent prayers.

units.la: Posthæc Deputatus regius monet, Regem per literas nominasse sex senatores regni, omnes fere nobiles, quibus tanquam suis assessoribus, Ius suffragii definitivi competeret. Responsum à Præside; Regem in publicis fidei literis à Marchione prolatis, nullam fecisse assessorum quorumlibet mentionem, provinciam deputationis soli Marchioni commendasse; rem esse pessimi exempli quæ plurima incommoda secum traheret, si assessoribus jus illud definitivi suffragii concedatur; qui hodie sex, eodem jure posse cras vel centum assessoribus idem jus afferere, qui pluralitate suffragiorum vel synodo renitente obtinerent quod regi consultum esset: Regem Iacobum, licet pluribus synodis interfuisset, unico tamen suffragio contentum fuisse; Neque haec a se dici volunt, quasi sinistri aliquid de nobilibus illis suspicarentur; verum studio vitandi praecipitia illa, ad quae antea naufragium ac libertatis jacturam passa est ecclesia: Contra haec omnia protestatur deputatus, protestationem synodi registris inseri petit; quod factum simul cum synodi responso.
units.tr: After this, the royal commissioner reminded them that the king, by letter, had named six senators of the kingdom, nearly all of them nobles, who as his assessors were to have the right of a definitive vote. The President replied that the king, in the public letters of credence presented by the Marquis, had made no mention of any assessors at all, and had committed the business of the deputation to the Marquis alone; that it was a matter of the worst example, which would bring many inconveniences with it, if that right of definitive vote were granted to assessors; for if six today, by the same right, tomorrow a hundred assessors could claim the same right, and by a majority of votes, even against the will of the synod, obtain whatever was pleasing to the king. King James, although he had attended several synods, had been content with a single vote. Nor did they wish this to be said as if they suspected anything sinister about those nobles; rather it was from zeal to avoid those dangers into which the Church had previously been wrecked and lost its liberty. The commissioner protested against all this, and asked that his protest be entered in the synod's registers; this was done together with the synod's reply.

units.la: (23. Novemb. sessione 3.)
units.tr: (23 November, third session.)

units.la: Actum fuit de electione Scribae seu actuarii, quem Scoti Clericum vocant: post prolixam & taediosam altercationem omnium fere suffragiis electus est Archibaldus Ihonstonus, Advocatus in suprema curia: eique a Sandilandio tradita fuerunt duo volumina manuscripta quae continent acta nationalium synodorum post annum 1590. Rogabat Praeses an ullus adesset cui aliquid cognitum esset de voluminibus praecedentium synodorum acta continentibus, ex quibus solis verus Ecclesiae Scoticae status cognosci posset; Sandilandius patris nomine sancte affirmabat; patri volumina illa nunquam visa fuisse, dolebant omnes tanti cimelii jacturam, ignari quomodo damnum illud resarciri posset: Tandem Ihonstonus novus synodi Scriba cum magno omnium gaudio, quinque volumina scripta aut signata manu eorum qui Scribae synodorum tum erant, protulit, quae continebant omnia acta Synodalia Ecclesiae Scoticae ab initio reformatae ibidem religionis, anno 1560. usque ad 1590, si acta quaedam exceperis, quae impia & audaci manu Pseudo-Episcopus Adamsonus expunxit, uti in palinodia sua ingenue est confessus. Proxima ergo cura fuit, ut de librorum horum ἀνθιστ[?] inquirerent, hæc autem provincia consentiente deputato regio, demandata est quinque provectioris ætatis pastoribus, quibus manus eorum qui tunc scribæ fuerunt, erat familiariter cognita, hisque adjuncti tres jurisperiti, seniores; Ac ut omnis fraudis vel levissima abesset suspicio, enixe rogabat synodus deputatum regium, ut tres regni Senatores laboris hujus essent inspectores; sed frustra.
units.tr: There was business concerning the election of a scribe or clerk (actuarius), whom the Scots call the Clerk. After a long and tedious dispute, Archibald Johnston, advocate in the Court of Session, was elected by almost all votes. Sandilands handed him two manuscript volumes containing the acts of the national synods after the year 1590. The Moderator asked whether anyone present knew anything of the volumes containing the acts of the earlier synods, from which alone the true state of the Scottish Church could be known. Sandilands solemnly affirmed, in his father's name, that his father had never seen those volumes, and all lamented the loss of so great a treasure, not knowing how the damage could be made good. At last Johnston, the new clerk of the synod, to the great joy of everyone, produced five volumes written or signed by the hand of those who had then been clerks of the synods. They contained all the synodal acts of the Scottish Church from the beginning of the reformed religion there, in 1560, down to 1590, except for certain acts which the pseudo-bishop Adamson struck out with an impious and bold hand, as he openly confessed in his palinode. The next task was to inquire into the authenticity of these books. With the royal commissioner agreeing, this business was committed to five older ministers, who were familiar with the handwriting of those who had then been clerks, and to them were added three senior lawyers. So that there might be no suspicion of fraud, however slight, the synod earnestly asked the royal commissioner that three senators of the realm should oversee this work, but in vain.

units.la: Post hæc agi cœptum est de examinandis literis fidei cum quibus deputati ab Ecclesiis ad synodum ablegati fuerant, quas Scoti vocabulo forensi Commissiones vocant; Deputatus regius instabat ut scriptum illud Episcoporum prius prælegeretur, cum quædam forte contineret quæ lucem aliquam discutiendis illis literis afferrent, quorum nullus esset usus post examinatas literas. Ecclesiarum vero deputati contra censebant, præmittendam esse literarum fiducialium examinationem; idque quia scriptum illud Episcoporum formalem protestationem contra omnia synodi membra, tanquam illegitime deputata, continere noverant, neque nudam solum præle-ctionem, quin potius ejusdem inter acta relationem, ac rationum contentarum examen statim intendi conjecturis non contemnendis colligebant, quod ante synodum in omnibus suis membris rite constitutam nisi cum manifesto ecclesiasticæ libertatis damno concedi non potuit.
units.tr: After this, business began on examining the letters of credentials with which the commissioners had been sent to the synod by the churches, which the Scots call by the legal term "commissions." The royal commissioner insisted that the bishops' paper be read first, since it might perhaps contain something that would throw light on examining those letters, a point that would be of no use once the letters had been examined. The commissioners of the churches, on the contrary, held that the examination of the letters must come first. They knew that the bishops' paper contained a formal protest against all the members of the synod as illegitimately commissioned, and they inferred, on no slight grounds, that its mere reading, or rather its entry into the minutes and an immediate examination of the reasons it contained, was intended to unsettle the synod. This could not be allowed before the synod was properly constituted in all its members, except with clear loss to ecclesiastical liberty.

units.la: Adde quod intempestiva hac scripti hujus prælectione, synodi progressum tantum non interturbare, ac judicandi & sententiam ferendi de membris suis potestatem hac arte synodo subreptam, in unicum deputatum regium cum dictatoria potestate conferre satagebant hierarchici: cui seniorum (ut vocant) laicorum præsentiam cum potestate definiendi in causis & synodis Ecclesiasticis non serendam persuaserant, ut eventus postea docuit. Quare unanimi sententia ab examinatione literarum fidei incipiendum esse dicunt, deputatoq; regio protestanti, responderunt; Non negari simpliciter scripti illius praelectionem, verum in tempus opportunum solummodo differri; nihil damni episcoporum causae dilatione hac necessaria illatum iri, quandoquidem in progressu examinis harum literarum, aut post examinatas literas exceptiones illas proponi liceret, quibus ad bonorum virorum arbitrium se satisfacturos spondent.
units.tr: Moreover, the prelatists were eager, by this untimely reading of the paper, to disrupt the progress of the synod. By this trick they hoped to take from the synod the power of judging and pronouncing on its own members and to transfer it to a single royal commissioner with dictatorial power. They had persuaded him that the presence of lay elders (as they call them), with power to decide in ecclesiastical causes and synods, was not to be tolerated, as the outcome later showed. Therefore, by unanimous vote, they declared that the examination of the letters of credence should begin. In reply to the protesting royal commissioner they answered that the reading of that paper was not simply refused but only deferred to a fitting time. No harm would come to the bishops' cause from this necessary delay, since in the course of examining these letters, or after they had been examined, those objections could be put forward, by which they promised to satisfy the judgement of good men.

units.la: (24. Novemb. Sess. 4.)
units.tr: (24 November, fourth session.)

units.la: Examinantur itaque quorundam deputatorum literae, quantum per temporis angustiam, & negotia alia intercurrentia fieri potuit, nam omnium literarum numerus excrevit ad 122. uno fere tenore & forma, quibus mandabatur, ut deputati ad locum Synodo destinatum tempore se conferrent, in eaque suo (i. e. deputantium) nomine, proponerent, disputarent, sententiam ferrent de rebus omnibus Ecclesiasticis quae sub ambitum liberae Nationalis Synodi veniunt, secundum Dei verbum & confessionem fidei publice in hoc regno receptam ac authoritate multarum Synodorum Nationalium identidem munitam. Postremum hoc consulto additum, non quod cuilibet scripto humano in se considerato parem authoritatem tribuant cum verbo Dei, sed quod pro orthodoxa consensus formula agnoscant, ex qua orta haec controversiae facilius dirimi possent; haec ad praecavendam eorum calumniam, qui simplicioribus ignaris saepe, quid rerum agatur persuadere satagunt, orthodoxos Scotos resorbere Antichristianas sordes, ac in Pontificiorum quos deseruerunt castra reditum meditari: Sed hoc solenne hominibus hisce sycophantarum intemperiis & maledicentiae aestro agitatis, criminum quibus laborant, ac quorum[?] manifesto tenentur, infamiam in innocentes per calumniam transferre, ut scilicet integritatem mentiantur, hoc est quod vulgo dici solet οἱ φάσεις [illegible, ~8 letters].
units.tr: Accordingly, the letters of some of the commissioners were examined, as far as the shortness of time and other intervening business allowed, for the number of all the letters had risen to 122. Almost all were in one tenor and form, by which the commissioners were ordered to present themselves at the place appointed for the synod at the proper time, and there, in the name of those who had sent them, to propose, debate, and pass judgement on all ecclesiastical matters that fall within the scope of a free National Synod, according to the Word of God and the confession of faith publicly received in this realm and repeatedly confirmed by the authority of many national synods. This last clause was deliberately added, not because they grant any human writing, considered in itself, authority equal to the Word of God, but because they acknowledge it as an orthodox formula of consensus, by which these controversies might more easily be settled. This was to forestall the slander of those who, often trying to persuade simple and ignorant folk of what is going on, claim that the orthodox Scots are swallowing back Antichristian filth and plotting a return to the camp of the Papists whom they deserted. But it is the habit of such men, driven by the frenzy of sycophants and the rage of slander, to transfer by calumny onto the innocent the infamy of the crimes they labour under and are manifestly guilty of, so that they may feign integrity themselves. This is what is commonly said of them.

units.la: Necessaria hac digressiuncula defunctus, ut ad semitam unde digressus revertar. Inter examinandum literas fidei, acres sæpius concertationes obortæ, quæ tamen synodi prudentia sæpe amicè sopitæ fuerunt. Harum nobilissima fuit inter duos Nobiles, Classis Brechinensis deputatos, quorum uterque literas deputatorias proferebat, dumque suas proferret Dunensis Comarcha, forte in tergo literarum quædam erant ad causæ hujus summam non pertinentia & imprudenter à Scriba synodi prælecta, quorum authenticum exemplar sibi tradi postulat deputatus regius; Ast synodus haud æquum judicabat privati cujuslibet scripti copiam dare, scripti præsertim domino reluctante, ac contranitente; ideo protestatur deputatus regius; quaprotestatione soluta est sessio hæc.
units.tr: Having finished this necessary digression, I return to the path from which I strayed. While the letters of credence were being examined, sharp disputes often arose, though the prudence of the synod often settled them amicably. The most notable of these was between two nobles, commissioners of the Presbytery of Brechin, each of whom produced letters of commission. While Lord Dun was producing his, some matter on the back of the letters, not relevant to the substance of this business, was imprudently read out by the clerk of the synod, and the royal commissioner demanded an authentic copy of it. But the synod did not think it fair to give a copy of any private writing, especially when its owner was reluctant and resisting. Therefore the royal commissioner protested, and with that protest the session was closed.

units.la: (26. Novemb. sess. 5.)
units.tr: (26 November, session 5)

units.la: Sedulo pergitur in reliquarum literarum examine: cui in hac sessione finis imponitur. Observatum fuit Classem Abredonensem in partes scissam fuisse duas, sed inæquales: Minor D. Robertum Baronium & D. Iacobum Sybaldum, SS. Theologiæ Doctores & Pastores Abredonenses, illum etiam ibidem professorem; delegabat: sed gravibus de causis irritam hanc deputationem declarat Synodus: utriusque tamen præsentiam mirum in modum desiderabat, præsertim cum scriptis editis labantem hierarchicorum causam fere soli sustinere conati fuerint: Absentiæ improvisæ causas scrutantibus varia occurrebant; & qui in horum mysteriorum abdita & recessus altius penetrabant, judicabant omnia hæc eorum consilio fieri, quorum suasu ulteriorem synodi progressum deputatus regius impediturus erat, conjecturamque hæc (ut multorum fuit opinio) magis probabilem fecit pastoris cujufdam audacia qui ex Roffia ad synodum fe ablegatum dicebat, quumque electionem suam à synodo irritam declarari cerneret æquissimis de causis, statim quam paratam habebat protestationem contra synodum totam, singulaque ejus fere membra prælegendam obtrufit, qua synodum illegitimam pronunciabat, ideo quod seniores Laicos ad suffragia admitteret, licet legitima vocatione instructos; & quod ad paftorum delegatorum electionem in Classibus admissi fuerint; hujus protestationis exemplar sibi tradi poftulat regius deputatus, ægreque tulit Andreæ Rami-sei, veterani pastoris, itidemque doctissimi, zelum, (quem quidam, Marchioni familiaris, tanquam vanam jactantiam ac bullatas nugas ipse Thrafoni haud multum dissimilis traducebat) quod obtulerit, paratum fe in arenam descendere, ac probaturum ex scriptura sacra, prima & incorrupta antiquitate, conciliis, consensu & quotidiana praxi omnium aliarum Ecclesiarum reformatarum, (Anglicanis non exceptis apud quas laici agnoscuntur judices ordinarii in foro celsæ commissionis, quod tribunal est ecclesiasticum) præter constantem Scoticarum ecclesiarum praxin ab ipsis reformationis incunabulis, Laicos quos vocant seniores non solum ad suffragia in synodis esse admittendos, verumetiam necessaria esse synodorum ecclesiasticarum præsertim nationalium membra, ac licet deputato regio adesset Theologus magni nominis, qui privatim multa in contrarium polliceretur, ac Episcoporum doctissimi in urbe aut vicino Hammiltonio hærentibus, ignota non potuit esse hæc provocatio; nèmo tamen conditionem certaminis seu publice seu privatim suscipere ausus fuit
units.tr: The examination of the remaining letters went on diligently and was brought to an end in this session. It was observed that the Aberdeen Presbytery had been divided into two parts, but unequal ones. The lesser part delegated Mr Robert Baron and Mr James Sibbald, Doctors of Sacred Theology and ministers of Aberdeen, Baron also being a professor there. But for serious reasons the Synod declared this delegation void. Nevertheless, it greatly missed the presence of both men, especially since they had tried, through printed writings, to support almost alone the tottering cause of the hierarchists. Those who inquired into the causes of their unexpected absence found various explanations. Those who penetrated more deeply into the hidden and secret workings of these affairs judged that all this was done on the advice of those by whose persuasion the royal commissioner was going to obstruct the further progress of the Synod. This conjecture became more probable (as was the opinion of many) because of the boldness of a certain minister who said he had been sent to the Synod from Roffia. When he saw his own election most justly declared void by the Synod, he at once thrust upon the assembly a protest, already prepared, against the whole Synod and against nearly each of its members, which he read aloud. In it he declared the Synod illegitimate, because it admitted lay elders to the votes, although they were lawfully called, and because men were admitted in the presbyteries to the election of delegated ministers. The royal commissioner demanded a copy of this protest to be handed to him. He took it badly that Andrew Ramsay, an old minister and a very learned man, showed such zeal (which some, a familiar of the Marquis, derided as empty boasting and bubbling trifles, the man himself being not much unlike Thraso). Ramsay offered himself as ready to enter the arena and to prove from Holy Scripture, from the earliest and uncorrupted antiquity, from the councils, from the agreement and daily practice of all the other reformed churches, not excepting the English, among whom laymen are recognised as ordinary judges in the court of high commission, which is an ecclesiastical tribunal, and besides the constant practice of the Scottish churches from the very beginnings of the Reformation, that the so-called lay elders are not only to be admitted to votes in synods, but are even necessary members of ecclesiastical synods, especially national ones. And although a theologian of great name was present with the royal commissioner, who privately promised much to the contrary, and although the most learned bishops, staying in the city or in nearby Hamilton, could not have been ignorant of this challenge, yet no one dared to accept the conditions of the contest, either publicly or privately.

units.la: (27. Novemb. seff. 6.)
units.tr: (27 November, session 6)

units.la: Quibus provincia inquirendi de ἀυθεντίας[?] voluminum illorum commissa fuit (quæ non fine singulari Dei providentia conservata, ac nunc tempore tam opportuno luci reddita fuerunt) judicium suum scripto exhibent, libros illos omnes & singulos genuinos esse, hujusque τεκμήρια[?] novemdecim, ex libris illis inter se collatis, proferunt, usque adeo evidentia, ut deputato regio publicam hanc vocem extorserint: multos animo suo rationum illarum evidentia scrupulos exemptos esse, licet rem certo vix sibi persuasam diceret. A reliquis vero ecclesiarum, Academiarum, ac urbium delegatis, omnes dubitationis nebulæ penitus abstersæ fuerunt, ita ut statim in rem judicatam tranfiffent[?], nisi præsesin[?] sequentem sessionem differendum censuisset, tum ut longioris moræ gratiam regio deputato faceret, tum ut nullis calumniandi posthac locus esset, rem tanti momenti præcipitatam fuisse.
units.tr: Those to whom the task of investigating the authenticity [αὐθεντίας] of those volumes was committed (volumes preserved by no small providence of God, and now brought to light at so opportune a time) present their judgment in writing. They declare that all those books, each and every one, are genuine, and they set forth nineteen proofs [τεκμήρια] drawn from comparing those books with one another. These proofs are so evident that they forced the royal commissioner to a public admission: that many doubts had been removed from his mind by the evidence of those arguments, although he said he was hardly persuaded of the matter with certainty. From the delegates of the other churches, academies and towns, every cloud of doubt was completely wiped away, so that they would at once have proceeded to a decision, had not the president thought fit to postpone the matter until the following session. This was done partly to grant the royal commissioner a favour of further delay, and partly so that there would be no opportunity hereafter to slander the matter of such weight as having been rushed.

units.la: Dein Præsidi proponenti, an Synodo placeret Assef-sorum[?] sibi adjungere? Respondit synodus, Assessorum consuetudinem nunquam hic usitatam fuisse, licere tamen Præsidi quos vellet nominare, quorum privatim indies uteretur opera in rebus præparandis & dirigendis: Ecquid, inquit præses, placet de privato colloquio? Non placere respondent omnes, memores quam improbe eo abusi fuerint hierarchici ad synodorum authoritatem enervandam. Nominati tum fuere quidam qui Præsidi essent à consiliis; aliis vero mandatum, ut ecclesiarum ad synodum gravamina colligerent, & disponerent, ac ordine proponerent. Atque tunc demum declaratur, integram esse synodum, in omnibus membris rite constitutam.
units.tr: Then the President asked whether it pleased the Synod to join assessors to himself. The Synod replied that the custom of assessors had never been used here, but that the President might name whom he wished, whose help he could privately use day by day in preparing and directing business. "Does it please you," said the President, "to have a private conference?" All answered that it did not please them, remembering how shamefully the hierarchists had abused such conferences to weaken the authority of the synods. Then some were named to be the President's counsellors, and others were ordered to collect the grievances of the churches for the Synod, and to arrange and present them in order. And only then was it declared that the Synod was complete, duly constituted in all its members.

units.la: Profertur scriptum illud ab Episcopis formatum; ac per Robertum Hammiltonium pastorem: (quem huic negotio specialem procuratorem statuerant Episcopi) synodi scribæ legendum tradit; subscri-bebatur bebatur manu sex quà Archiepiscoporum quà Episcoporum. Eo praelecto nobiles quidam (qui synodo aderant non ut deputati, sed ut actionem contra Episcopos prosequerentur): instrumenta (ut vocant) authentica sibi concedi postulant, Episcopos scripto hoc agnoscere se citatos, cum per procuratorem comparerent, quem apud acta citant ut de die in diem synodo se sistat acturus delegantium Episcoporum causam, quorum voluntariam absentiam causae suae fraudi non futuram quo minus contra eos tanquam praesentes agatur, rogant. Quibus à deputato regio responsum est: Scriptum illud sibi non synodo destinatum; quaestionem esse de judicis competentia, quae exceptio haberi debet peremptoria: mandat etiam procuratori ne synodo se sistat. Praelecta fuerant eadem sessione tria alia scripta, signata paucorum quorundam concionatorum manu; sed quia quicquid in omnibus est notatu dignum, fusius in Episcoporum protestatione continetur, illius praecipua capita subjungam.
units.tr: That writing, drawn up by the bishops, was produced, and through Robert Hamilton, a minister (whom the bishops had appointed as their special procurator for this business), it was handed to the Synod's clerk to be read. It was subscribed by six hands, of archbishops and of bishops. When it had been read, certain nobles (who were present at the Synod not as delegates but to carry on the action against the bishops) asked that authentic instruments, as they are called, be granted to them, to show that the bishops had acknowledged by this writing that they were summoned. For when they appeared through a procurator, whom they named in the records, the bishops promised that he would present himself to the Synod from day to day to plead the cause of the bishops who had sent him. They asked that the voluntary absence of the bishops should not harm their cause, so that the case might proceed against them as if they were present. To these men the royal commissioner replied that the writing was not addressed to the Synod; that the question concerned the competence of the judge, which exception ought to be held as peremptory; and he also ordered the procurator not to present himself before the Synod. In the same session three other writings had been read, signed by the hands of a few preachers. But since whatever is worth noting in all of them is set out more fully in the bishops' protest, I shall append its principal heads.

units.la: Episcoporum protestatio contra Synodum.
units.tr: The Bishops' protestation against the Synod.

units.la: Licet(inquiunt) synodos Nationales legitime convocatas & constitutas, malis quibus vexatur ecclesia removendis, pacisque stabiliendae necessaria & effi-cacia esse media ingenue fateamur, ac jus convocandi easdem ad regem solum pertinere profiteamur, absque cujus consensu & approbatione si qui in synodum coire ausi fuerint non solum eos seditionis, verum etiam imminuti juris regii reos putamus; Conventum tamen hunc Glasguensem pro legitima synodo habendum non esse hisce ratio-nibus demonstramus: 1. Quia delegatorum si non omnes, saltem plurimi, electi fuerant ante indictam regia authoritate synodum: 2. Quia pastores deputati pro veris pastoribus habendi non sunt, cum non subscripserint confessioni fidei in præsentia Archiepiscoporum, Episcoporum, Superintendentium, aut Commissariorum, neque coram iisdem Fidelitatis ac Primatus, sive supremitatis juramentum regi præstiterint, uti legibus municipalibus hujus regni cautum fuit Iacob. 6. parlament 3. cap. 46. anno 1572. 3. Quia confessioni fidei à rege mense Septembri labentis hujus anni imperatæ subscribere pertinaciter detrectarunt: 4. Quia dignitatem & privilegium Episcoporum, (qui primum ordinum regni seu parlamenti membrum constituunt) petulanter impugnarunt, quod frequentibus regni legibus gravissimis læsæ majestatis criminibus accensetur: 5. Quia licet præcedentium criminum infamia non tenerentur, à presbyteriis tamen seu Classibus deputati sunt, qui se omni authoritate deputatos ad synodum delegandi privarunt: utpote quod abjectis ac remotis præsidibus suis ab Episcopis constitutus (quod synodo Glasguensi anno 1610. Episcopis concessum fuit) alios inconsultis Episcopis substituerint: 6. Quia horum deputatorum electioni in presbyteriis adfuerunt æquali numero & authoritate seniores laici, ut plurimum Nobiles magnæ authoritatis, quibus facile fuit pastores (in quibusdam etiam locis numero pauciores) in suam sententiam vel invitos metu pertrahere: ita ut ecclesiarum ad hanc synodum deputati, potius dicendi sunt, Delegati laicorum quam Cleri; quod non solum ordini, decoro, & receptæ per totum Christianum orbem laudabili consuetudini, verumetiam praxi & consuetudini hujus Ecclesiæ Scoticæ adversatur, nam nullus est qui affirmet quadraginta annis præteritis apud nos locum concessum fuisse in Classibus seu presbyteriis, senioribus illis laicis, præsertim dum de electione delegandorum ad synodum Nationalem ageretur; 7. Quia delegati pastores seditiosis & tribunitiis concionibus, honori regio detraxerunt, subditosque ad rebellionem excitarunt: 8. Quia alii schismatici sunt, ordini & decoro nulla pacis habita ratione, pervicaciter se opponentes: perjuri, canonicam ordinariis Episcopis obedientiam detrectantes, ad quam praestandam juramento solenni astricti sunt; censura Ecclesiae Hibernicae & Scoticae notati; Omnes fere merito à sacri ministerii functione deponendi:
units.tr: Although (they say) we frankly admit that national synods lawfully convoked and constituted are necessary and effective means for removing the evils that trouble the Church and for establishing peace, and although we profess that the right to convoke them belongs to the king alone, so that if anyone has dared to gather in a synod without his consent and approval we judge them guilty not only of sedition but also of diminishing the royal right, we nevertheless demonstrate by these reasons that this Assembly at Glasgow is not to be held a lawful synod: (1) because the delegates, if not all, at least most of them were chosen before the synod was announced by royal authority; (2) because the deputed ministers are not to be regarded as true ministers, since they did not subscribe the confession of faith in the presence of the Archbishops, Bishops, Superintendents or Commissaries, nor take before them the oath of fidelity and of primacy, or supremacy, to the king, as the municipal laws of this kingdom provide, James 6, Parliament 3, chapter 46, in the year 1572; (3) because they stubbornly refused to subscribe the confession of faith enjoined by the king in September of this present year; (4) because they wantonly attacked the dignity and privilege of the Bishops, who constitute the first order of the kingdom and a member of Parliament, an offence which by the frequent laws of the realm is counted among the gravest crimes of treason; (5) because, although they were not bound by the infamy of the earlier crimes, they were deputed by the presbyteries or classes, which had deprived themselves of all authority to delegate deputies to the synod, since, having cast off and removed their presidents appointed by the Bishops (a power granted to the Bishops by the Glasgow synod of 1610), they substituted others without consulting the Bishops; (6) because in the election of these deputies in the presbyteries there were present, with equal number and authority, lay elders, mostly nobles of great authority, by whom it was easy to draw the ministers (in some places even fewer in number) into their opinion, even against their will; so that the deputies of the churches to this synod should rather be called delegates of the laity than of the clergy. This conflicts not only with order, decorum and the praiseworthy custom received throughout the Christian world, but also with the practice and custom of this Scottish Church, for there is no one who will affirm that in the past forty years any place was granted among us in the classes or presbyteries to those lay elders, especially when the election of delegates to the National Synod was under discussion; (7) because the deputed ministers, by seditious and tribune-like sermons, have detracted from the king's honour and stirred up the subjects to rebellion; (8) because others are schismatics, stubbornly opposing without any regard to order, decorum or peace; they are perjured, refusing the canonical obedience to the ordinary Bishops which they are bound by solemn oath to render; they are marked by the censure of the Irish and Scottish Churches; and nearly all of them deserve to be deposed from the function of the sacred ministry.

units.la: 9. Quia senioribus laicis jus suffragii definitivi conceditur, quod an in Ecclesia bene ordinata & constituta ferendum sit, ostendit veterum Conciliorum praxis. Hinc illud patrum quarti oecumenici Concilii Chalcedonensis: Mitte foras superfluos; Theodosii junioris vox est Christiano Principe digna, dicentis, Illegitimum esse eum qui non sit in ordine sanctissimorum Episcoporum ecclesiasticis immiscere tractatibus: Mandavit etiam Pulcheria imperatrix Stratego, ut Clerici, laici, monachi, ut repellerentur, exceptis paucis illis quos Episcopi secum duxerunt: unde quoque vox illa Martini in Concilio Chalcedonensi; Non esse suum, sed Episcoporum tantum subscribere: Et quid vetat quominus nos iisdem verbis deputatum regium compellemus?
units.tr: (9) Because the right of definitive vote is granted to lay elders, and whether this is to be tolerated in a well-ordered and properly constituted Church is shown by the practice of the ancient councils. Hence that saying of the Fathers of the fourth ecumenical Council of Chalcedon: "Send out the superfluous ones." The words of Theodosius the Younger are worthy of a Christian prince, saying that it is illegitimate for one who is not in the order of the most holy Bishops to meddle in ecclesiastical business. The Empress Pulcheria also ordered Strategius that clerics, laymen and monks should be driven out, except for the few whom the Bishops brought with them. Whence also comes that saying of Martin at the Council of Chalcedon: "It is not for them, but only for the Bishops, to subscribe." And what prevents us from addressing the royal deputy in the same words?

units.la: 10. Quia omnes fere deputati ante synodum hanc coactam aperte professi sunt se ea damnare, quae in Synodo discutienda & dijudicanda sunt, videl. Episcopatum; quinque articulos Perthenses; Clericorum politicas functiones, munia civilia; & hujus generis similia: quis autem æquos eos judices futuros exspectet, qui non solum arroganter praejudicarint ea de quibus in synodo agendum erit, verumetiam solennibus juramentis ad causas sic praejudicatas tuendas se obstrinxerint? Notum est inter multas recusati concilii Tridentini rationes à primis Reformationis promotoribus, hanc facile primariam fuisse, quod Pontifices Romani, qui se supremos judices judices venditarunt, diplomatis suis, Lutheri doctrinam haereticam declaraverint ante indictum illud Concilium: & quod Episcopi, judicum partes in concilio acturi, jurejurando & solennibus pactionibus ad Pontificis Romani dignitatem & dogmata tuenda, astricti fuerint: 11. Quia contra ipsos Archiepiscopos & Episcopos hostili & plusquam Vatiniano odio feruntur, cujus documenta peti possunt ex probroso illo citatoriarum literarum libello, impudentissimis & ad solam invidiam confictis criminationibus referto, horum suasu in omnibus regni ecclesiis publice praelecto, ut nobis omnibus infamiam & odium populi crearent; contra charitatem fraternam & Apostoli monitum, Seniorem ne increpato, sed hortare ut fratrem; contra statuta regni municipalia, vetantia ne contra quodlibet parlamenti membrum proferatur, quod ad dignitatis debitae diminutionem facere possit; contra canones synodorum nationalium prohibentes ne pro concione pastores quemquam nominatim perstringant, atque ne quilibet super inquirendis criminibus citetur; cum tamen libellus ille citatorius ad nullum speciale crimen descendat, aut reos designet: contra juris praxin receptam, quae vetat ne judicium aut sententia contra pastores proferatur, nisi prius trinae reorum citationes legitimae praecedant: Adde quod necesse sit citationes ab eo foro emanare, in quo causa disceptanda erit, quod de diffamatoriis hisce citationibus dici nequit; cum synodus tunc aperta nondum fuerit: denique libello eo omnes nos pari criminum omnium infamia notant, eorundemque atrocium, a quibus quam longe absimus vel ipsorum conscientiam attestamur: 12. Quia publice declaraverunt, Archiepiscopis, Episcopis qua talibus non deberi jus suffragii in synodis, nisi legitima vocatione a presbyteriis instruantur; Paradoxon certe absurdissimum, puriori & primitivæ Ecclesiæ Christianæ incognitum. 13. Quia Primati jus præsidendi negant, contra veterum Conciliorum statuta. Concilii primi Niceni can. 6. & Antiocheni can. 9. & Imperatorum rescripta, in Novella Iustiniani, constitutione 123. cap. 10: ac jus regni hujus municipale ac Synodorum nationalium constitutiones annorum 1606. 1608. & 1610. Si cui vero scrupulus hæreat ex constitutionibus Synodi 1600. ad Montis Rosarum, quasi præsidentia hæc Episcopis prohiberetur, quia statuit ne pastores ad jus suffragii de Republica in publicis Comitiis regni admittendi, in conventibus ecclesiasticis quid supra reliquos pastores sibi arrogent, Sciat (inquiunt Episcopi) omnes illas cautiones antiquatas esse, ac nobis Episcopis competere jus illud plenum dignitatis Episcopalis, quo unquam aut hic aut alibi gaudebant aut fruuntur Episcopi; synodorum constitutionibus, ac ordinum regni statutis declaratum esse; Quare cum posteriora derogent prioribus, æquum est ut his obliteratis illa religiose observentur: Si cui hoc non placet, sciat tamen dignitatem nostram Episcopalem instabili synodorum aut parliamentorum fundamento non niti; sed Christo cui soli supereminentiæ & exortis in Clerum nobis subditum potestatis gratiam debemus; sicuti regi (quem in omnibus subditorum quorumlibet causis solo Deo minorem agnoscimus,) dignitates & beneficia temporalia accepta referimus: At nunc pulchro hoc ordine inverso, liceat Cypriani verbis uti lib. 3. epist. 14. Quod non (inquit) periculum metuere debemus de offensa domini, quando aliqui de presbyteris, nec euangelii nec loci sui memores, sed neque futurum Dei judicium neque præpositum sibi Episcopum cogitantes, (quod nunquam omnino sub antecessoribus nostris factum est) cum contumelia & contemptu præpositi totum sibi vendicent. Atque utinam non prostrata fratrum salute sibi omnia vendicarent. Contumelias episcopatus nostri dissimulare & ferre possum, sicut dissimulavi semper & pertuli, sed dissimulandi nunc locus non est, quando decipiatur fraternitas nostra à quibusdam vestrum, qui, dum sine ratione restituendæ salutis plausibiles esse cupiunt, magis la-psis obsint. 14. Denique cum pastores omnes Episcopis minores sint, eorum judices in synodis sedere non possunt, quanto minus miscellaneus hic cœtus ex pastoribus & laicis conflatus: Quare nili Episcoporum omnium, nostram, ac successorum, quin & Ecclesiæ hujus causam silentio prodere velimus, Synodus hæc nobis recusanda est: Interim ne quis hoc a nobis fieri suspicetur, quasi reatu nocentis conscientiæ publicorum judiciorum lucem & examen subterfugeremus, Deum testem invocamus nihil nobis gratius futurum, quam ut in libera & legitima synodo, in qua illis solis judicibus locus sit, quos veterum Conciliorum canones (videlicet Chalcedonensis can. 9. Milevitani can. 22. & secundi Chartaginens. cap. 10.) Episcoporum judices decrevere: Aut coram te (Illustrissime Deputate) aut quolibet à rege ad id muneris delegato, causam nostram dicamus; quod si impetremus, confidimus nos facile morum nostrorum innocentiam ac dogmatum orthodoxiam, contra hostium nostrorum calumnias defensuros: Interim cum protestamur, cœtum hunc omnibus modis illegitimum esse, declaramus nostro, & Ecclesiæ Scoticæ nomine, nihil quod ab eo cœtu emanaturum sit, Canonis ecclesiastici authoritatem habere, posse aut debere; nec quod ab eo fiet in nostrum, aut alicujus reforma-tæ ecclesiæ præjudicium, Ecclesiæ Scoticæ imputandum esse; Profitemur nos adhærere religioni reformatæ, confessionique Ecclesiæ Scoticæ statutis parlamentariis insertæ, omnesque contrarios errores & hæreses damnare: deniq; ut ecclesia per Episcopos regatur, non solum legitimam gubernationis formam, sed necessariâ judicamus: &c. Hæc summa fuit prolixi istius scripti, Londini postea typis excusi, additis quibusdam quæ in responsione & judicio Synodi de hac protestatione notabuntur ad sessionis septimæ finem. Posthæc excerpta quædam prælegi jussit præses, quibus locū & jus suffragii in synodis præsertim nationalibus senioribus deberi afferebatur: ulterioremq; tractationem sera nox interrupit.
units.tr: (10) Because almost all the deputies, before this synod was called, openly declared that they condemned those matters which are to be discussed and judged in the Synod, namely the episcopate, the Five Articles of Perth, the political functions of the clergy, civil offices, and other things of this kind. Who, then, would expect those men to be fair judges, who not only arrogantly prejudged the matters on which the synod is to act, but also bound themselves by solemn oaths to defend causes so prejudged? It is well known that among the many reasons for refusing the Council of Trent given by the first promoters of the Reformation, this was easily the chief: that the Roman Pontiffs, who boasted of being the supreme judges, had by their decrees declared the doctrine of Luther heretical before that Council was called; and that the Bishops, who were to act as judges in the council, had been bound by oath and solemn pacts to uphold the dignity and dogmas of the Roman Pontiff. (11) Because they bear a hostile and more than Vatinian hatred against the Archbishops and Bishops themselves, of which proofs may be sought in that scandalous libel of citation, crammed with most shameless accusations invented only to stir up envy. At their urging it was publicly read in all the churches of the kingdom, so as to create infamy and hatred for us all among the people. This is contrary to brotherly charity and the Apostle's admonition, "Do not rebuke an elder, but exhort him as a brother"; contrary to the municipal statutes of the kingdom, which forbid that anything be put forward against any member of Parliament which could diminish his due dignity; contrary to the canons of the national synods, which forbid ministers to name anyone by name in a sermon, and forbid anyone to be cited "to inquire into" crimes; although that citatory libel descends to no specific crime and designates no accused persons; contrary to the received practice of law, which forbids any judgment or sentence against ministers to be pronounced unless three lawful citations of the accused have first preceded it. Add that citations must issue from the court in which the case is to be argued, which cannot be said of these defamatory citations, since the synod was not yet open at that time. Finally, by that libel they all mark us with an equal infamy for all crimes, and we attest before God, and their own conscience, how far we are from those atrocities. (12) Because they have publicly declared that the right of suffrage in synods is not owed to Archbishops and Bishops as such, unless they are admitted by lawful summons from the presbyteries. This is certainly a most absurd paradox, unknown to the purer and primitive Christian Church. (13) Because they deny the right of presiding to the Primate, contrary to the decrees of the ancient councils: canon 6 of the First Council of Nicaea, canon 9 of Antioch, and the rescripts of the emperors in Justinian's Novella 123, chapter 10; and contrary to the municipal law of this kingdom and the constitutions of the national synods of 1606, 1608 and 1610. But if anyone is troubled by a scruple arising from the constitutions of the Synod of 1600 at Montrose, as if this presidency were forbidden to Bishops, because it decreed that ministers should not be admitted to the right of voting on public affairs of the realm in the public assemblies, let them know (say the Bishops) that all those cautions are abolished, and that the full right of episcopal dignity belongs to us Bishops, the right which Bishops here or elsewhere have ever enjoyed or do enjoy; this has been declared by the constitutions of synods and the statutes of the orders of the kingdom. Therefore, since the later provisions derogate from the earlier, it is fair that the earlier ones, being blotted out, should be religiously observed. If anyone does not like this, let him know nonetheless that our episcopal dignity rests not on the unstable foundation of synods or parliaments, but that we owe it to Christ alone, who gave us the supremacy and the grace of power over the clergy subject to us; just as we credit the king (whom we acknowledge as lesser than God alone in all the causes of his subjects, of whatever kind) with our temporal dignities and benefices. But now that this fine order is inverted, let me use the words of Cyprian, book 3, letter 14: "We ought not to fear the danger of offending the Lord when some of the presbyters, mindful neither of the gospel nor of their place, nor thinking of the future judgment of God or of the Bishop set over them (which never at all happened under our predecessors), claim everything for themselves with insult and contempt for their superior." And would that they did not claim everything for themselves while the salvation of the brethren lies prostrate! I can bear and overlook the insults to our episcopate, as I have always overlooked and endured them; but there is now no room for overlooking, since our brotherhood is being deceived by some of you, who, while they desire to be plausible in restoring salvation without reason, do more harm to the fallen. (14) Finally, since all the ministers are lesser than the Bishops, they cannot sit as judges of the Bishops in synods, much less this motley assembly made up of ministers and laymen. Therefore, unless we wish to betray in silence the whole cause of all the Bishops, of ourselves, of our successors, and indeed of this Church, this synod must be refused by us. Meanwhile, lest anyone suspect that we do this as if, conscious of guilt, we were shunning the light and examination of public judgments, we call God to witness that nothing would be more welcome to us than to plead our cause in a free and lawful synod, in which only those judges have a place whom the canons of the ancient councils (namely Chalcedon canon 9, Milevis canon 22, and the Second Council of Carthage chapter 10) have decreed as judges of Bishops. Let us plead our cause either before you, most illustrious Deputy, or before whomever the king may delegate to this office. If we obtain this, we trust that we shall easily defend the innocence of our conduct and the orthodoxy of our doctrine against the calumnies of our enemies. Meanwhile, while we protest that this assembly is in every way illegitimate, we declare in our own name and in the name of the Scottish Church that nothing which proceeds from that assembly can have, or ought to have, the authority of an ecclesiastical canon; nor is anything done by it to our prejudice, or to the prejudice of any reformed church, to be imputed to the Scottish Church. We profess that we adhere to the reformed religion and to the confession of the Scottish Church inserted in the parliamentary statutes, and that we condemn all contrary errors and heresies; and finally, we judge that the Church should be governed by Bishops, not only as a lawful form of government but as a necessary one, etc. This was the substance of that lengthy writing, afterwards printed at London, with some additions which will be noted in the response and judgment of the Synod on this protestation at the end of the seventh session. Afterwards the president ordered certain excerpts to be read, by which it was asserted that a place and a right of suffrage in synods, especially national ones, were owed to the elders; and a late night interrupted the further discussion.

units.la: (28. Novemb. sess. 7.)
units.tr: (28 November, session 7)

units.la: Agitur de libris illis continentibus nationalium synodorum acta ab initio reformatæ religionis ad annum 1590: An [?]κεφάλαια[?] illa & 19. rationes pro [?]αὐτοκεφαλίας[?] prolatæ omnibus satisfacerent ? instabat Deputatus regius, ac publice protestabatur, ne quid præjudicii majestati regiæ, aut Episcopis afferret judicium Synodi, quam ad librorum approbationem propendere videbat; cum quædam se habere diceret libris illis objicienda: Responsum fuit à Nobiliss. Comite Rothusio, (ab Ecclesiis in Fisana provincia, cui hæreditarius vicecomes præest, deputato) exceptiones illas jam proponendas; quibus synodum statim responsuram spondet. Tandem cum nihil à quolibet prolatum esset, omnium deputatorum calculis approbantur libri illi, ac declarantur esse vera, genuina Ecclesiæ Scoticæ regiftra, ac pro talibus usquequaque citra contradictionem habenda. Agnoscebant omnes non sine singulari Dei providentia libros illos tam auspicato luci jam redditos, majorique gaudio perfusi fuere omnium animi, quod de illis jamdudum conclamatum esset, speque omni excidissent, thesaurum illum quinquaginta hactenus annis sublatum aut delitescentem recuperandi, præsertim cum ignotum non esset, quanta semper sollicitudine laboraverint hierarchici, primitivam ecclesiæ hujus politiam exterorum etiam celeberrimorum scriptis commendatam (quæ nunc ex hisce libris solis depromi potuit) supprimendi. Inter varios de hisce sermones, locum insignem, ex præfatione præfixa syntagmati confessionum reformatæ ecclesiæ, prælegendum censuit præses; quo egregium disciplinæ apud Scotos tunc receptæ testimonium perhibetur, nihil veritus mercenariorum & mordacium sannionum insulsas sannas, quibus statutum est futili dicacitate proscindere, quæcunque quæstui cui se devoverunt, officere possunt.
units.tr: The discussion turned to the books containing the acts of the national synods from the beginning of the reformed religion down to 1590. The question was whether the "heads" [κεφάλαια] and the nineteen reasons put forward for autocephaly [αὐτοκεφαλίας] would satisfy everyone. The royal deputy pressed the point and publicly protested that the synod's judgment should cause no prejudice to the royal majesty or to the bishops. He saw that the synod was inclined to approve the books, but he said that he had some objections to bring against them. The Most Noble Earl of Rothes, deputed by the churches of the province of Fife, over which he presides as hereditary sheriff, replied that those objections should be put forward now, and he promised that the synod would answer them at once. In the end, since no one brought forward anything, the books were approved by the votes of all the deputies and declared to be true and genuine records of the Scottish Church, to be held as such everywhere without contradiction. All acknowledged that by a singular providence of God these books had at last come to light, and every heart was filled with great joy. People had long given up hope of recovering that treasure, which had been removed or hidden for some fifty years. This was especially so because it was well known how constantly the prelatists had laboured to suppress the primitive polity of this Church, which had been commended in the writings even of celebrated foreigners and could now be drawn from these books alone. Among the various remarks made on the subject, the president thought fit to read a notable passage from the preface prefixed to the collection of confessions of the reformed Church. In it is given an outstanding testimony to the discipline then received among the Scots. He did not fear the silly jeers of hired and biting scoffers, who with their empty wit seek to tear to pieces whatever might hinder the profit to which they have devoted themselves.

units.la: Deinde cœptum est agi de protestatione Episcoporum, an rationes recusatæ synodi validæ essent: duas vero illas, in quibus arcem causæ suæ ponebant Episcopi, (videlicet 1. Quod synodus esset pars adversa: 2. Quod Senioribus jus suffragii concederet) primum agitandas proponit præses. Porro cum prima exceptione usos fuisse Remonstrantes Belgicos in celeberrima Synodo Dordracena omnibus compertum esset; responsionem Theologorum magnæ Britanniæ prælegit & expositit, quorum sententia fuit, Non valere ad synodi authoritatem enervandam, quod causentur Remonstrantes, maximam Synodi partem constare ex adversariis suis; neque jus naturale permittere, ut qui adversarius est, in causa sua sedeat; & putamus ministros, etiamsi contrariam sententiam publice docuerint, ac defenderint, posse nihilominus, & (quandoquidem legitime vocati sunt) debere sedere judices in causa Remonstrantium examinanda & dijudicanda: Nec posse Remonstrantes ullo jure illorum in hac Synodo congregatorum authoritatem declinare: Quod cum densa argumentorum acie munierint celebres illi Theologi, ac in eandem sententiam ab omnibus aliis Theologis exteris uno ore itum fit, mirari se dicebat, cur cramben hanc reponerent Episcopi. Tum loquendi veniam præfapraefatus D. Gualterus Balcanquellus, Decanus Rof-sensis in Anglia, ac Subaudiani nosocomii, quod Londini est, Rector &c. à rege Iacobo ad synodum Dordracenam ecclesiarum Scoticarum nomine (iisdem tamen non consultis) olim missus, Multis ostendere conabatur, quam dispar esset comparatio inter Remonstrantes Dordracenam synodum recusantes, & Episcopos hujus synodi judicium declinantes; Duas notabat differentias: prima (inquit) est, quod controversiae in synodo Dordracena agitatae, fuerint de doctrinae dogmatibus, iisque fundamentalibus, quo casu Theologis neutralibus esse nunquam licet, cum iis ex officio incumbat, nova contra receptam ecclesiae doctrinam dogmata spargentibus, omni conatu obstistere: Ast alia ratio controversiarum hic ventilandarum, cum non sint de fidei doctrina sed de disciplina, quam Scoticarum Ecclesiarum confessio articul. 21. Mutabilem judicat: quare cum in his judicium suum in alteram partem propendere ante coactam synodum declaraverint pastores, ipso facto jus omne postmodum de illis controversiis judicandi in synodo amiserunt. Secunda vero disparitas hinc oritur, quod Pastores Belgici ad synodum illam delegati, licet privatis sermonibus, publicis concionibus, & libris etiam editis declaraverint Remonstrantium dogmata sibi non placere, nunquam tamen eo processerunt, ut sententia aliqua judiciali eadem damnarint, multo minus sacramentis, aliisque sanctis pactionibus ad alteram controversiae partem se obligarint, aut in capita fautorum contrarii dogmatis conjurarint, prout à delegatis ad hanc synodum factum esse queruntur Episcopi. Ad haec à Praeside responsum. Controversias omnes, praesertim si quinque controversiarum articulorum limites non excedant, inter Remonstrantes & Contraremonstrantes, non fuisse, esse de dogmatibus fundamentalibus: erasse quidem Remonstrantes graviter, verum nondum sibi Persuasum omnes heterodoxias esse haereses: Deum non negare se, art. confessionis citato disciplinam dici mutabilem: verum illud de Accidentanis circumstantiis de quibus nihil statuerit verbum Dei esse intelligendum. Nam disciplinæ essentialia (h. e. quæ Apostoli authore Spiritu S. ecclesiis erudiendis præscripta reliquerunt) in mutabilium censum non retulisse confessionis illius authores, demonstrabat. Etenim ejusdem articul. 19. Disciplina ad amussim verbi Dei efformata, post verbum & sacramenta, tertia ecclesiæ verę visibilis nota dicitur; unde sequitur, licet non sit ἀπλῶς [?] necessaria ad ecclesiæ τὸ εἶναι, ita ut quæcunque ecclesia disciplinam verbo Dei in omnibus conformem non habeat, ea pro vera Christi ecclesia habenda non sit; Absit à nobis tam procax censura; relinquenda hæc antiquis Donatistis & hodiernis Anabaptistis, eorumque genuinis furculis hodiernis: licet, inquam, simpliciter necessaria non sit ad esse, necessaria tamen est ad ecclesiæ visibilis integritatem & perfectionem necessaria etiam ad ecclesiam, à posteriori saltem indicandam, medium denique & adjumentum ordinarium sine quo non ita facile ecclesiæ salus obtineri possit: Quam necessitatem cum anno 1528. negaret Robertus Montgomerius Pseudoarchiepiscopus Glasguensis, disciplinamque mutabilem statueret, graves eo nomine ecclesiæ Scoticæ pœnas dedit: Quæ, si demonstrandæ immutabilitatis eorum quæ disciplinæ essentialia sunt, non sufficiant; saltem succurrat quod in actis Synodi Nationalis ad annum 1596. relatum est: Quæsitum tum fuit an liceret principi aut pastoribus dubia movere de disciplinæ externis articulis, de quibus nihil expresse haberetur in S. Scriptura vel affirmativè vel negativè: Responsum fuit à synodo, licere principi per se aut per legatos suos proponere de quo dubitat, seu quod reformandum censuerit in specie externi ordinis; id etiam cuivis licere, modo studiis modestis, decenter, loco & tempore debitis, animo ædificandi non tentandi id fiat: Porro addit quædam esse extra dubitationis & controversiæ aleam ponenda, dum subjungit hæc verba: Quandoquidem substantia externæ administrationis ecclesiasticæ plenissime in scripturis tradita sit: qua clausula, accidentalia licet mutabilia judicarit synodus pro circumstantiarum varietate, quo sensu articulus ille confessionis intelligendus est, esse tamen in disciplina ἀκίνητα quædam, declarat: Ac de his non de illis litem inter Episcopos & Ecclesias esse, ipsi Episcopi non negant, statuentes regimen ecclesiæ per Episcopos necessarium, à Christo institutum; cuius mandata omnes ubique & semper ligant: Itaque nullam esse primam illam inter Episcopos & Re-monstrantes Belgicos disparitatem facile quivis inferet. Addebat alius David Dogelisius Cupri Fifani pastor: Vocari in judicium Episcopos, quod plurimas Pontificiorum heterodoxias, & Remonstrantium errores (ut mollissime dicam) privatim foveant & publicè promoverint, quos cum ipse D. agnoscat esse fundamentales, eorum saltem ratione parem esse rationem Episcoporum & Remonstrantium, cum facinus quos inquinat, æquet. Sed detur (inquiebat) quæstionem esse de solis disciplinæ capitibus, iniquum certe esset pastores ad synodum hanc delegatos privare jure dicendi sententiam in synodo, cum de illis judicabitur, de quibus ante convocatam synodum rotunde & aperte sententiam dixerunt: Exemplo sit Ecclesiæ praxis contra Novatum & Donatum schismaticos, quorum heterodoxiæ & in disciplina ecclesiastica errores ab iis in synodo damnati fuerunt, qui ante coastas synodos, quà privatim, quà publicè masculè sese iis opposuere: Adde quod si soli neutrales possunt esse hic judices, nullus autem sit in Ecclesia Scotica pastor, qui non ostenderit se in alterutram controversiæ partem inclinare, ubi quæso harum controversiarum judices quærendi sunt? Si extraneas & transmarinas ecclesias consulendas dixeris, eodem laborabit hæc sententia incommodo, & ad eundem lapidem offendere necesse erit: Præterquàm quod sic nullæ fere ecclesiæ ad componendas lites in se enatas essent idoneæ. Ad secundam differentiam paucis respondit Præses; nec magno certe conatu opus fuit longis ejusmodi logis refellendis, cum, primo intuitu, comparationem hanc æquâ lance librantibus, Remonstrantibus in hac causa tam similes esse Episcopos, quàm lac lacti simile esse, conspicuum sit. Quod autem de sacramentis quibus se obstrinxerunt ad synodum delegati contra Episcopos; fuse ad id in responso synodi ad Episcoporum protestationem respondebitur. De secunda vero Episcoporum exceptione, An senioribus jus suffragii definitivi in synodis competat? nulla fuit disputatio, cum præses, ut ansam argutiis omnibus ineptis præcideret, sic propositum controversiæ statum, An senioribus, statutis ecclesiæ Scotiæ, jus suffragii competat? Et sic finis isti controversiæ impositus fuit, cum nullus prodiret seniorum jus impugnaturus.
units.tr: Next it was taken up to consider the bishops' protest, whether the reasons for refusing the synod were valid. The president proposed to deal first with the two grounds on which the bishops rested the chief part of their case, namely (1) that the synod was a party to the dispute, and (2) that it granted a right of voting to the elders. As to the first exception, it was known to all that the Remonstrants of the Low Countries had used it at the famous Synod of Dort. He read out and explained the reply of the divines of Great Britain, whose opinion was this: "It does not weaken the authority of the synod that the Remonstrants complain that most of the synod consists of their adversaries. Natural law does not allow one who is an adversary to sit in judgment in his own cause. We think that ministers, even though they have publicly taught and defended the contrary opinion, can nevertheless, and indeed (since they were lawfully called) must, sit as judges in examining and deciding the cause of the Remonstrants. Nor can the Remonstrants by any right decline the authority of those gathered in this synod." Since those famous divines had fortified this position with a dense array of arguments, and since all the other foreign divines had agreed with one voice on the same view, the speaker said he wondered why the bishops were bringing up this old stale matter again. Then, asking leave to speak, Mr Walter Balcanquell, Dean of Rochester, Rector of the Savoy hospital in London, who had once been sent by King James to the Synod of Dort in the name of the Scottish churches (though without consulting them), tried to show at length how unequal the comparison was between the Remonstrants, who refused the Synod of Dort, and the bishops, who decline the judgment of this synod. He pointed out two differences. The first, he said, is that the controversies discussed at the Synod of Dort concerned doctrinal points, and fundamental ones at that. In such a case theologians may never be neutral, since it is their duty to resist with all their effort those who spread new doctrines against the received teaching of the Church. But the nature of the controversies to be aired here is different, since they concern not the doctrine of faith but discipline, which the Confession of the Scottish Churches, article 21, judges to be changeable. Therefore, since the ministers had declared before the synod was convened that their judgment inclined to the other side, they had by that very fact lost all right of judging these controversies afterwards in the synod.
