Cum liceat, rebus Ecclesiæ sic urgentibus, in synodum vetante licet magistratu convenire; prout firmiter à se demonstratum dicunt tum in tractatu, eade re edito mense Iunio, tum in responsione ad praefationem protestationis Episcoporum, Certe potiori jure licet synodum a magistratu supremo indictam, inchoatam, praesentia Deputati regii septem integris diebus cohonestatam, in omnibus suis membris legitime constitutam; continuare; extrema ecclesiae necessitate id flagitante; praesertim cum nullo Canone Ecclesiastico aut statuto parlamentario, aut superioris aevi exemplo ostendi possit, potestatem dissolvendi synodum ad lubitum regi concessam fuisse; quare multo minus concedendum Deputato regio, cui secundum commissionis exhibitae tenorem, sola potestas indicendi synodum ac in eadem sedendi secundum legem & praxin tradita fuit. Idem a majoribus suis factitatum esse: uti ex publicis Ecclesiarum regiftris constat: Nam licet Anno 1582. Synodi nationalis Andreapoli coactae dissolutio a deputato & senatoribus regiis severe mandata esset, nisi a proscriptione causae contra Montgomerium Pseudo-Archiepiscopum Glasguensem protinus desisterent, Synodum tamen constanter in causae iustius examinatione progressam esse, & damnato Montgomerio, regi ac senatoribus per literas significasse, quam periculosa eorum consilia essent, qui regia authoritate abutuntur, ad hanc ecclesiarum libertatem ejusmodi interdictis opprimendam: quam a Christo concessam, juri regio non derogare declarant saepius statuta parlamentaria, praesertim anni 1592. Et cui tutandae solenni sacramento se obstrinxit Serenissimus Rex regnum hoc ante quinquennium initurus: Porro si mandato huic morem gessisset Synodus tempore tam importuno, facile judicatu est, in quantas malorum myriades ecclesiam & regnum conjecisset.
units.tr: On the eleventh point, that they continued this assembly in defiance of the order to dissolve it, they reply: since the Church's affairs are so pressing, it is lawful to meet in synod even when the magistrate forbids it. They say they have firmly demonstrated this both in the treatise published in June on this very matter and in the answer to the preface of the Bishops' protestation. Certainly, by a stronger right, it is lawful to continue a synod that was called and begun by the supreme magistrate, graced by the presence of the king's deputy for seven full days, and lawfully constituted in all its members, especially when the extreme necessity of the Church demands it. No ecclesiastical canon, parliamentary statute, or precedent from earlier times can show that the power to dissolve a synod at the king's pleasure was ever granted. Much less, then, is it to be conceded to the king's deputy, to whom, by the terms of his commission, only the power to call a synod and to sit in it according to law and practice was given. Their predecessors did the same, as is clear from the public registers of the Churches. For although in 1582, when a national synod was gathered at St Andrews, the king's deputy and senators strictly ordered its dissolution unless they at once abandoned the prosecution of the case against Montgomery, the pseudo-archbishop of Glasgow, the synod nevertheless continued steadily in the more just examination of the cause. Having condemned Montgomery, it informed the king and the senators by letter how dangerous were the designs of those who abuse royal authority to crush, by such prohibitions, this liberty of the Churches, which Christ granted and which, they declare, does not derogate from the royal right, as the parliamentary statutes have often declared, especially that of 1592. Nor does it derogate from the solemn oath by which the most serene King bound himself to defend it, when he was about to take up this kingdom five years ago. Moreover, had the synod obeyed this order at so unseasonable a time, it is easy to judge into how many myriads of evils it would have plunged the Church and kingdom.

units.la: Quod ad illa edicto regio subjecta, declaratio videlicet impunitatis, & protectionis eorum quibus synodus... synodum hanc recusantibus, damni quidpiam illatum erit. Cum prima (inquiunt) facie tantam iniquitatem præ se ferant, non posse sibi persuaderi, à Rege optimo prodiisse, nisi dolo & calumniis adversariorum prius circumvento, quorum rea conscientia latebras quærens, tutelam sæcularis brachii implorat, ut debitas manifestis sceleribus pœnas effundiat: Etenim cum jure divino non minus clavium, & jurisdictionis potestas, quam prædicandi verbum & sacramenta administrandi Ecclesiæ, & Synodo eandem repræsentanti competat, Matt. 8. Dic Ecclesiæ, & si Ecclesiam audire neglexerit, & cæt.
units.tr: As to those points subjoined to the royal edict, namely the declaration of impunity and protection for those who... [refuse] this synod, some loss will be inflicted. They say that at first sight these points show such great iniquity that they cannot persuade themselves that they came from the most good King, unless he had first been circumvented by the trickery and calumnies of his adversaries. Their guilty conscience, seeking hiding places, implores the protection of the secular arm so that it may pour out the punishments due to manifest crimes. For by divine right the power of the keys and of jurisdiction belongs no less to the Church, and to the synod representing it, than the power of preaching the Word and administering the sacraments: "Tell it to the Church; and if he neglect to hear the Church," Matt. 18, and so on. [Matt. 8 as printed.]

units.la: 1. Cor. 5. & Apocalyps. 2. Reprehenduntur Ecclesiæ Pergami & Theatyræ, quod segniores fuerint in exercenda Ecclesiastica censura contra Baalamitas, Nicolaitas, & Iezabelem: eadem nequit suspendi, multo minus tolli authoritate qualibet humana: Potestatem hanc libere exercuerunt Ecclesiæ Apostolicæ & Primitivæ, ejusque exercitium impedientibus, responsum. Deo potius quam hominibus auscultandum. Act. 4. Addunt, lege civili, Canonica, ordinaria praxi regnorum omnium, quæ plane barbara non sunt, fancitum esse, si quid contra jus & utilitatem publicam impetratum fuerit, ei obtemperandum non esse, sed rejiciendum ut furto subreptum, & per mendacium postulatum: quod de Antiocho refert Plutarchus, & de aliis imperatoribus historici plures. Videantur utriusque juris Doctores in titulo de Rescriptis: & causa 25. quæst. 2. sæpius: Porro citationibus hujusmodi Iuris Canonici, se illud minime approbare dicunt libertatis vindices, quod Antichristo unde primitus processit, ad cujus hierarchiam stabiliendam collimat, relinquunt; verum id à se fieri in gratiam Episcoporum, quibus impunum illud jus unice in delitiis est; & argumento, ut loquuntur, ad hominem: Eandem semitam terunt, regni hujus statuta municipalia. Iacobi 6. Paral.6. statuto 92a & parlam. 11. statut. 47. Præsertim vero stat. 106. parl. 7. Iacobi 6, anno 1581. quibus expresse mandatur, supremarum curiarum judicibus, ut in omnibus causis quæ ad illa fora pertinent dijudicandis, intrepide procedant; easdemque sublata omni cunctatione definiant, latamque sententiam executioni mandent, non obstante quolibet Regis mandato aut rescripto in contrarium: nihilque quotidiana hujus praxi in curiis illis usitatius: nam nisi singula causarum genera ad proprium forum referantur, mera obtinebit ἀτελία, ac nisi curiis illis supremis libertas hæc illibata constet, sub umbra promovendi jus regale, regnaret injustitia: Quæ eum locum habeant in sæcularibus curiis; potiori jure synodo nationali legitime convocatæ & formatæ competunt; utpote cui, supremam potestatem controversias omnes ecclesiasticas determinandi afferant vel ipsi Hierarchici, Theologi videl. Magnæ Britanniæ ad Synodum Dordracenam deputati, in judicio suo de Remonstrantium protestatione: qua sententia non putabant se juri regio detrahere, aut Papatui in Synodi persona renovare, quæ opinionem hanc nunc modeste tuentibus atrociter objiciuntur, ab iis qui struunt de proprio calumnias innocentiæ; & quod nondum auf sunt Antiqui Papatus monstrum aperta facie omnibus adorandum reponere, sub velo supremorum Magistratuum obtrudunt, eorumque spiritu bestiam illam extrema spirantem, refocillare, ejusque vulnera mortalia obligare, nequicquam satagunt. Denique ad illud quo omnibus mandatur subscriptio fœderis & confessionis juxta sensum & Declarationem à Marchione Regis nomine publicatam, Respondent; Sensum illum non esse genuinum, sed confessioni affixum, contrarium publicæ professioni & praxi majorum Confessioni primitus subscribentium anno 1580 & 1590. prout latius demonstrabitur ad seff. ubi declaratio illa diligentius excutietur. Quare Synodus tota tum ecclesiarum omnium Scoticarum nomine quas repraesentat, tum suo, protestatur. 1. Unicum hunc oculis suis obiectum fuisse scopum, ad quem omnia studia collimarunt, videl. ut solidam ecclesiae pacem restituerent, cui promovendae iis solummodo legitimis mediis se instituisse, quae Dei verbum & laudabiles Ecclesiae hujus constitutiones monstrarunt: Deum etiam cordium scrutatorem testem esse, quam sincero animo in hoc toto negotio se gesserint, & quam liberae sint omnium conscientiae ab aliquo criminis reatu in regiam majestatem. 2. Sibi licitum fuisse & esse, Synodum hanc regia authoritate indictam, & in membris suis rite constitutam continuare; quoad unanimi Deputatorum consensu dissolvetur. 3. Conventum hunc esse in se, ac ab omnibus habendum esse, pro legitima, plenissima, & liberrima synodo nationali: ejusque constitutionibus aequum esse ut omnes, qui se hujus ecclesiae membra haberi volunt, modeste se submittant, ac mediis omnibus legitimis honorem & obedientiam procurent 4. Probris & convitiis atrocibus, quibus seu edicto hoc, seu alibi synodus haec immerito petitur, ejusdem honorem non laesi: utpote quae plena hac responsione dilucide abstersa sint, praesentibus hisce citare se regios senatores, qui edicto huic de dissolutione synodi subscripserunt, aut quovis modo ratum habuerunt, ut in proximo Parliamento se sistant, perniciosi hujus consilii rationem reddituri regi ac regni ordinibus, uti cautum est expressa lege Iacob. 4. Parl. 2. statuto. 12. §. Si quid incommodi oriatur, violenta impeditione ne synodo huic sua sarta tecta constet authoritas, illud non sibi imputandum esse, sed praesulibus eorumque asseclis, qui sicut omni conatu Synodi convocationem impediverunt, sic convocatam aspernati sunt, ac portentofis suis protestationibus plauftra convitiorum in eam immerentem jactarunt, ac tandem veriti, ne in apricam lucem omnium oculis spectanda prodiret ipsorum impietas & perfidia, salfis & fictis criminationibus obtinuerunt mandatum hoc dissolutionis: quare eos solos esse Ecclesiasticae pacis turbones, regni incendiarios, libertatis ecclesiasticae invasores, & oppressores; omnium denique malorum, fi quae consecutura sint (quae avertat Deus) reos, & cæt.
units.tr: "1 Cor. 5" and "Rev. 2": the Churches of Pergamos and Thyatira are rebuked because they were too slack in exercising ecclesiastical censure against the Balaamites, the Nicolaitans and Jezebel. That censure cannot be suspended, much less removed, by any human authority whatever. The apostolic and primitive Churches exercised this power freely, and to those who hindered its exercise they answered that God must be obeyed rather than men (Acts 4). They add that by civil law, canon law, and the ordinary practice of all kingdoms, which are not altogether barbarous, it is established that if anything has been obtained against right and the public good, it is not to be obeyed but rejected as stolen by fraud and procured by lying. Plutarch reports this of Antiochus, and many historians of other emperors. Let the doctors of both laws be consulted under the title on rescripts, and cause 25, question 2, often. Yet by citing such canon law they say that as champions of liberty they by no means approve it, since it has come forth from Antichrist, toward whose hierarchy it aims; they leave it to him. They do this, however, for the sake of the bishops, to whom that unpunished right is their sole delight, and as an argument, as they put it, ad hominem. They tread the same path with the municipal statutes of this kingdom: James 6, Parl. 6, statute 92a, and Parl. 11, statute 47; and especially statute 106, Parl. 7, James 6, of the year 1581. These expressly order the judges of the supreme courts to proceed fearlessly in deciding all cases that belong to those courts, to settle them without any hesitation, and to carry out the sentence pronounced, notwithstanding any royal command or rescript to the contrary. Nothing is more common in the daily practice of those courts. For unless each kind of case is referred to its proper forum, mere immunity [ἀτελία] will prevail, and unless this liberty remains unimpaired for those supreme courts, injustice would reign under the pretext of advancing the royal right. If these things hold in the secular courts, they hold with still greater reason for a national synod lawfully convened and constituted, to which the supreme power of determining all ecclesiastical controversies belongs. Indeed, the very theologians of Great Britain sent to the Synod of Dort, in their judgment on the protestation of the Remonstrants, asserted this. They did not think they were thereby detracting from the royal right, or reviving Popery in the person of the synod. Yet those who now modestly uphold this opinion are fiercely charged with it by men who plot calumnies against innocence on their own account. And since they have not yet dared to set the ancient monster of Popery openly before everyone to be worshipped, they try in vain to foist it upon us under the veil of the supreme magistrates, and to revive by their spirit that beast breathing its last and to bind up its mortal wounds. Finally, to the point that everyone is ordered to subscribe to the covenant and the confession according to the sense and declaration published by the Marquis in the king's name, they reply that this sense is not genuine but was attached to the confession, contrary to the public profession and practice of those who first subscribed the confession in 1580 and 1590, as will be shown more fully at the session where that declaration is examined more carefully. Therefore the synod, both in the name of all the Scottish Churches it represents and in its own, protests: 1. that the single aim before its eyes, toward which all its efforts were directed, was to restore solid peace to the Church; that to advance this it employed only those lawful means which the Word of God and the laudable constitutions of this Church pointed out; and that God, the searcher of hearts, is witness with what sincere mind they conducted themselves in this whole matter, and how free their consciences are from any guilt of crime against the royal majesty. 2. That it was and is lawful for them to continue this synod, called by royal authority and duly constituted in its members, until it is dissolved by the unanimous consent of the deputies. 3. That this assembly is in itself, and must be held by all, a lawful, fully authorized and most free national synod; and that it is right that all who wish to be counted members of this Church should modestly submit to its decrees and by all lawful means promote its honour and obedience. 4. That the honour of this synod is not harmed by the disgraceful and atrocious reproaches with which it is unjustly assailed, whether in this edict or elsewhere, since these have been clearly wiped away by this full answer. Moreover, they summon, through these presents, the royal senators who subscribed to this edict for the dissolution of the synod, or in any way approved it, to appear at the next Parliament, there to render an account of this pernicious counsel to the king and the orders of the kingdom, as is provided by the express law of James 4, Parl. 2, statute 12, §. "If any inconvenience arises." 5. That if the synod's authority is not kept whole and intact by violent hindrance, this is not to be imputed to them, but to the prelates and their followers. As they used every effort to prevent the synod's convening, so, once it was convened, they scorned it, and with their monstrous protestations they hurled carts full of insults against an undeserving body. Finally, fearing that their own impiety and perfidy would come to light and be seen by everyone's eyes, they obtained this order of dissolution by false and fabricated accusations. Therefore they alone are the disturbers of ecclesiastical peace, the incendiaries of the kingdom, the invaders and oppressors of ecclesiastical liberty, and, in sum, answerable for all the evils that may follow, which God forbid, and so on.

units.la: Sessio 9. Novemb. 30. Die Veneris.
units.tr: Session 9. November 30, Friday.

units.la: Ad examen revocantur praecedentes aliquot Conventus ecclesiastici videl. Limnuchenses duo, annorum 1606 & 1608. Glasguensis 1610. Abredoniensis 1616. Andreapolitanus 1617. Perthanus 1618. An habendi essent legitimae Synodi nationales: Multa tum in medium prolata fuerunt à compluribus pastoribus veteranis, quibus illegitimas esse demonstrabant: Ac ne rem tanti momenti praecipitasse diceretur Synodus; quibusdam à se publice designatis provinciam committunt, registra Synodalia diligenter excutiendi; ut quam cito fieri posset, ex registris illis excerpta fideliter scripto exhiberent, ut mature de iisdem despiceret Synodus.
units.tr: Several earlier ecclesiastical assemblies are brought under examination: namely the two at Linlithgow, of 1606 and 1608; Glasgow, 1610; Aberdeen, 1616; St Andrews, 1617; and Perth, 1618. The question is whether they were to be held as lawful national synods. Many things were then brought forward by several veteran ministers, by which they showed that these assemblies were unlawful. So that it could not be said the Synod had rushed a matter of such importance, it committed the task of carefully searching the synodal registers to certain men whom it publicly named, so that they might, as quickly as possible, present in writing extracts faithfully taken from those registers, and the Synod might consider the matter in due time.

units.la: Decemb. 1. Sessio 10. Die Saturni.
units.tr: December 1. Session 10. Saturday.

units.la: Designati ad Ecclesiarum gravamina colligenda, synodi judicio discutiendam proponunt Causam presbyterii seu classis Edenburgensis contra Davidem Mitchelium, pastorem Edenburgenum, in jus vocatum, quod omnes Remonstrantium hæresias, & complures Pontificiorum hæreses publice pro Concione defenderit, hujusque ecclesiae doctrinam in Confessionibus publicis contentam petulanter exagitarit: complurium testimoniis dilucide proba-tum tum fuit, quod novam illam liturgiam, antiquata veteri, ecclesiis inconsultis & repugnantibus praelegerit, Cumque classis judicium subterfugiens, ad Synodum nationalem provocaverit, eam itidem aspernatus fit, Episcoporum protestatione[?] contra Synodum subscribens: ob quod contumaciæ crimen, licet alia abessent, Depositionisà ministerii functione & excommunicationis censura notandus esset; secundum expressam constitutionem Synodi nationalis Andreapolitanæ anni 1582. Ex eodem luto factum fuisse D. Pantherum seu Panitarium. S S. Theologiæ professorem in Academia Andreapolitana compertum fuit; Gladstono autem Archidiacono Andreapolitano, ejusque ecclesiæ pastori præter Contumaciam adversus Synodum, objectum fuit ordinariæ ebrietatis scandalum & vitæ profanitas: Quos tres supradictorum criminum reos & convictos teneri liquido probatum fuit:
units.tr: Those appointed to collect the grievances of the churches propose, for the judgment of the synod, the case of the presbytery or classis of Edinburgh against David Mitchel, minister of Edinburgh, who was summoned before it. He had publicly defended from the pulpit all the heresies of the Remonstrants and several heresies of the Papists, and had insolently attacked the doctrine of this church as contained in the public Confessions. By the testimony of several witnesses it was clearly proved that he had read out that new liturgy, with the old one set aside, against the wishes and objections of the churches. When he evaded the judgment of the classis and appealed to the national synod, he likewise scorned that synod, subscribing a protest of the bishops against it. For this crime of contumacy, even if there were no other charges, he deserved to be deposed from the ministerial office and marked with excommunication, according to the express constitution of the national synod of St Andrews of 1582. Likewise, Dr Panther, or Panitarius, professor of sacred theology in the University of St Andrews, was found to be from the same mud. Gladstone, archdeacon of St Andrews and minister of its church, was charged, besides his contumacy against the synod, with the scandal of habitual drunkenness and a profane life. It was clearly proved that these three were guilty of the above-mentioned crimes and were held convicted.

units.la: Sess. 11. Decemb. 3. Die Lunæ.
units.tr: Session 11. December 3. Monday.

units.la: Post doctam & accuratam heterodoxiarum Arminianarum refutationem, institutam per Davidem Dicksonum Irwinensis ecclesiæ pastorem, sententia depositionis à functione pastorali in Davidem Mitchelium concordibus omnium suffragiis lata est: exhibitæ fuerunt literæ Episcopi Orcadum ad synodum; quibus absentiam suam in ætatem provectam, morbum, itineris difficultates hyberno hoc tempore conjiciebat, pollicitus synodi judicio se submissurum: Designati fuerunt quidam quibus tanquam Synodi deputatis commissum fuit causas pastorum Edenburgensium & aliorum in vicino illo tractu cognoscere post synodum dimissam.
units.tr: After a learned and careful refutation of the Arminian heterodoxies, carried out by David Dickson, minister of the church of Irvine, a sentence of deposition from the pastoral office was passed against David Mitchel by the unanimous votes of all. Letters from the bishop of Orkney were presented to the synod, in which he excused his absence on account of his advanced age, illness and the difficulties of travel in this winter season, promising to submit to the judgment of the synod. Certain men were appointed to whom, as deputies of the synod, was committed the task of hearing, after the synod had been dismissed, the cases of the ministers of Edinburgh and of others in that neighbouring district.

units.la: Sess. 12. Decemb. 4. Die Martis.
units.tr: Session 12. December 4. Tuesday.

units.la: Post nervosam & solidam dogmatum Arminianorum refutationem, per Robertum Bailium Kilwininæ ecclesiæ pastorem; accusantur pastores quidam corruptæ Doctrinæ & violentæ compulsionis auditorum suorum ad praxin novarum ceremoniarum aliorumque criminum, eorumque causa ad Synodi delegatos refertur. Una omnium voce Gladstono pastore Andreapolitano, cujus accusationis capita prælecta & examinata fuerant sessione præcedenti, omni ecclesiastico munere prorsus interdicitur.
units.tr: After a vigorous and solid refutation of the Arminian doctrines, delivered by Robert Baillie, minister of the church of Kilwinning, certain ministers are accused of corrupt doctrine and of forcing their hearers violently to practise new ceremonies, and of other crimes; their cases are referred to the delegates of the synod. By the unanimous voice of all, Gladstone, minister of St Andrews, whose articles of accusation had been read out and examined in the previous session, is altogether forbidden every ecclesiastical function.

units.la: Quibus provincia commissa fuit registra synodalia excutiendi, ut constaret an sex præcedentes synodi nationales (de quibus sessione 9. mentio facta fuit) essent legitimæ; rationes synodo proponunt, quibus prælectis, ac perpensis, uno ore, cum ad suffragia ventum esset, declarant, esse Pseudo-synodos, destitutas fere omnibus conditionibus ad liberam nationalem synodum constituendam necessariis: ab initio nullius authoritatis fuisse, nec deinceps earum statuta pro Synodi Canonibus habenda: rationes decreti hujus synodici hæ fuere.
units.tr: To those to whom the task was committed of examining the synodal records, in order to establish whether the six preceding national synods (of which mention was made in session 9) were lawful, they set out their reasons to the synod. When these had been read out and weighed, and when the matter came to a vote, they declared with one voice that they were pseudo-synods, lacking almost all the conditions necessary for constituting a free national synod: that from the beginning they had no authority, and that their statutes were not to be held as canons of the synod thereafter. The reasons for this synodical decree were these.

units.la: Synodus illa Limnuchensis anno 1606 habita, non fuit legitima; 1. quia justum tempus non interveniebat inter ejus indictionem & aperturam; utpote, indicta 3. Decemb. & aperta 10. ejusdem mensis, cujus defectu nec potuerunt à singulis classibus deputati delegari præsertim longius remotis; nec debite à propinquioribus gravamina formari. 2. quia multi admissi fuerant ad jus suffragii, qui ab Ecclesiis minime delegati fuerant, sed literis regiis de episcoporum consilio, evocati. 3. Quia literæ regiæ, quibus evocabanturqui isti conventui intererant; nullam faciunt Synodi nationalis mentionem: verum privati conventus in quo deliberandum solum esset de rebus ad Ecclesiæ commodum pertinentibus. 4. Idcoque Presbyteria deputatis suis hos limites posuisse; videlicet, ne suffragia ferrent tanquam in nationali synodo. ne assensum præberent cuilibet propositioni, cujus decisio ad Nationalem synodum pertineret; aut quae damnum quodlibet disciplinae receptae afferret; 5. quia ejus acta in libris synodicis non sunt inserta. 6. ideoque sequens synodus hanc pro nationali minime habuit; verum pro Colloquio ad deliberandum instituto.
units.tr: That synod held at Linlithgow in 1606 was not lawful: (1) because no proper interval lay between its summons and its opening, since it was summoned on 3 December and opened on 10 December of the same month, and for want of this interval the deputies could not be chosen from the individual classes, especially from the more distant ones, nor could grievances be duly drawn up by those nearer at hand; (2) because many were admitted to the right of voting who had not been sent by the churches at all, but were summoned by royal letters on the advice of the bishops; (3) because the royal letters by which those men were summoned to that gathering make no mention of a national synod, but speak of a private assembly in which only matters pertaining to the good of the church were to be deliberated; (4) and therefore the presbyteries set these limits on their deputies: namely, that they should not give votes as if in a national synod, nor give assent to any proposition whose decision belonged to a national synod, nor anything that would harm the discipline received; (5) because its acts were not inserted in the synodal books; (6) and therefore the following synod did not regard this as a national one at all, but as a colloquy instituted for deliberation.

units.la: Limnuchensis ista altera anno 1608. Ad jus suffragii admisit 42. nobiles ab ecclesiis, liberis civitatibus, ac Academiis non deputatos; ut pluralitate suffragiorum quod vellent tunc primum Episcopatuum exuviis onusti, impetrarent: 2. quia, licet secundum Canonem synodicum Taodunensem anni 1597. à singulis presbyteriis tres pastores cum seniore delegandi essent; hic à quibusdam quatuor, ab aliis plures mittuntur pastores, absentibus omnibus senioribus, utpote non vocatis.
units.tr: That other Linlithgow synod, of 1608, admitted to the right of voting forty-two nobles who had not been deputed by the churches, free towns and universities, so that, laden with the spoils of the episcopacies, they might obtain by a majority of votes whatever they wished, for the first time. (2) Although, according to the synodal canon of Dundee of 1597, three ministers with the senior were to be sent from each presbytery, some sent four, others more ministers, all the seniors being absent as not having been summoned.

units.la: Glasguensis anno 1610. non fuit legitima nationalis synodus. 1. quia deputatorum electio non fuit libera, sed restricta ad eos quos rex per literas nominatim designabat: 2. quia nulli ibi vocati fuerunt seniores ecclesiarum. 3. quia à quamplurimis presbyteriis plures pastores deputabantur, quam Canones ecclesiastici statuunt. 4. quia ad jus suffragii admissi fuerunt 30. Nobiles ab Ecclesiis non deputati, simul cum novis istis Pseudo-episcopis. 5. quia suffragia non fuerunt libera; sed extorta spe præmii liberaliter promissi; aut terrore indignationis regiæ.
units.tr: The Glasgow synod of 1610 was not a lawful national synod. (1) Because the choice of deputies was not free, but restricted to those whom the king named individually by letter; (2) because no seniors of the churches were summoned there; (3) because from very many presbyteries more ministers were deputed than the ecclesiastical canons allow; (4) because thirty nobles not deputed by the churches were admitted to the right of voting, together with those new pseudo-bishops; (5) because the votes were not free, but extorted by the hope of a reward generously promised, or by the terror of royal displeasure.

units.la: Abredoniana anno 1616. 1. quia præsidem non habuit suffragiis deputatorum electum: 2. quia defectu legitimæ præmonitionis non aderant omnes quorum intererat. 3. quia 24. Nobiles à Rege evocati, pastores quidam à presbyteriis non delegati, suffragia tulerunt. 4. quia exclusi fuerunt Ecclesiarum seniores. 5. quia conventus istius decreta PseudoArchiepiscopi Andreapolitani manu propria, aucta, deleta ac interpolata fuerunt.
units.tr: The Aberdeen synod of 1616: (1) because it did not have a president chosen by the votes of the deputies; (2) because, for want of lawful forewarning, not all whose interest was involved were present; (3) because twenty-four nobles summoned by the king, and certain ministers not sent by their presbyteries, gave votes; (4) because the seniors of the churches were excluded; (5) because the decrees of that gathering were altered, added to, erased and interpolated by the hand of the pseudo-archbishop of St Andrews himself.

units.la: Andreapolitana anno 1617. 1. quia nulla illius mentio habetur in libris synodicis. 2. quia rex ipse in literis ad subsequentem Perthensem synodum; Cœtum solummodo vocat, 3. quia informalitates & defectus omnium præcedentium Pseudo-synodorum hic concurrebant.
units.tr: The St Andrews synod of 1617: (1) because no mention of it is found in the synodal books; (2) because the king himself, in his letters to the subsequent synod at Perth, calls it only a gathering; (3) because all the informalities and defects of the preceding pseudo-synods met together here.

units.la: Perthensis anno 1618. Legitima non fuit. 1. quia defectu tempestivæ præmonitionis, multiadesse non potuerunt: utpote viginti solum dies indictio præcessit aperturam. 2. quia præsidis officium sibi arrogaverat Pseudo-archiepiscopus Andreapolitanus; 3. quia illegitime electus fuit Synodi scriba. 4. quia quinque integræ Diœceses aberant, videlicet, Orcadum, Catanesiæ, Rossiæ, Argatheliæ, Insularum: 5.[?] quia 19. Nobiles suffragia tulerunt, Item 11. Episcopi, ab Ecclesiis neutri deputati: cumque statuto synodico cautum esset ut singulæ civitates liberæ unum solummodo deputatum delegarent; & Edenburgum duos; hic tamen 36. civitatum deputati aberant, & ab aliis, quæ Episcoporum gratiâ venabantur, duo aut tres mittuntur. 6. quia nulli seniores à presbyteriis deputati aderant. 7. quia suffragium tulerunt pastores quidam nulla legatione legitima instructi, vel supra justum deputandorum numerū emissi. 8. quia pastores quidam à presbyteriis legitimè deputati, exclusi fuerunt à suffragio ferendo. 9. quia suffragia non fuerunt libera sed vel gravissimis extorta interminationibus carceris, exilii, abdicationis à ministerii functione, ni articulis istis quinque, quos rex obtrudebat, assensum protinus præberent vel spe lautioris stipendii expressa; alii vero deputatorum, fallacibus Episcoporum promissis circumducti fuerunt; si in decretum consentirent, praxin illorum articulorum liberam permansuram. Adde, quod publice tum profitebantur Episcopi, nec rationibus quibuscunque contrariis, nec suffragiorum numero locum futurum, si articuli isti non probarentur, utpote quos rex propria authoritate, inconsultis omnibus, imperaret. 10. Denique posthabito Dei verbo, Confessionibus fidei publicis, & legitimarum præcedentium synodorum canonibus, unicum ferendorum suffragiorum fundamentum & regula proponebatur, Mandatum, videlicet, regium; quod tum ex formali quæstionis tum propositæ statu, tum ex decretorum ipsorum formula conspicuum est:
units.tr: The Perth synod of 1618 was not lawful. (1) Because, for want of timely forewarning, many could not be present, since the summons preceded the opening by only twenty days. (2) Because the pseudo-archbishop of St Andrews had arrogated to himself the office of president. (3) Because the clerk of the synod was elected unlawfully. (4) Because five entire dioceses were absent, namely Orkney, Caithness, Ross, Argyll and the Isles. 5.[?] Because nineteen nobles gave votes, and likewise eleven bishops, none of them deputed by the churches; and whereas the synodal statute had provided that each free town should send only one deputy, and Edinburgh two, yet here deputies of thirty-six towns were absent, and from others which were hunting for the bishops' favour two or three were sent. (6) Because no seniors deputed by the presbyteries were present. (7) Because certain ministers gave votes who were furnished with no lawful commission, or were sent beyond the just number of deputies. (8) Because certain ministers lawfully deputed by their presbyteries were excluded from giving a vote. (9) Because the votes were not free, but were extorted either by the most severe threats of prison, exile, or removal from the ministerial office, unless they immediately gave assent to those five articles which the king was imposing, or by the express promise of a more generous stipend; while others of the deputies, led about by the deceitful promises of the bishops, were told that if they consented to the decree, the practice of those articles would remain free. Add that the bishops then openly professed that neither any contrary arguments nor the number of votes would have any place, if those articles were not approved, since the king commanded them on his own authority, with all consulted or not. (10) Finally, with the word of God set aside, the public Confessions of faith, and the canons of the preceding lawful synods, the only foundation and rule for giving votes that was put forward was the royal mandate, as is plain both from the formal state of the question as proposed and from the very wording of the decrees.

units.la: Sess. 13. Decemb. 5.[?] Die Mercurij.
units.tr: Session 13. 5 December (?). Wednesday.

units.la: Quandoquidem præcedentis sessionis decreto, conventibus istis Synodi nationalis Authoritas adempta esset; immediata & evidenti consequentia offendebat præses, corruere novitates omnes quibus ecclesia onerata fuit istarum Pseudo-synodorum prætextu: & juramentum illud in ministerii solemnibus à pastoribus præstitum, quo se obstringebant ad novitates illas tuendas: & cæt. Cumque ad suffragia ventum esset, unanimiter respondent omnes, Juramentum illud non obligare: cum certum sit pastores qui in juramentum illud à Pseudo-episcopis adacti fuerunt, supposuisse aliquod factum quod revera se ita non habeat, videlicet; Ecclesiam commisisse Episcopis potestatem adigendi in tale juramentum initiandos ministerii functione; ac novitates illas legitimarum synodorum authoritate introductas fuisse; ac nisi hæc ita se habuisse crediderint non fuisse juraturos: Nunc autem cum constet dolo malo elicitum fuisse ab Episcopis; quibus potestas hæc nunquam ab Ecclesiis concessa fuit, & vero constet synodos istas illegitimas esse; declara-rat synodus juramenta illa esse irrita, neque præstanda esse. Declarat etiam licitum semper fuisse presbyteriis, synodis provincialibus, omnes jurisdictionis Ecclesiasticæ actus, præsertim in admissione, & abdicatione pastorum, exercuisse ; quandoquidem nullius legitimæ synodi authoritate potestas hæc iis adempta fit : aut circumscribi possit.
units.tr: Since the decree of the previous session had taken away the authority of these meetings of the National Synod, the president saw an immediate and obvious consequence: all the innovations with which the Church had been burdened under the pretext of these pseudo-synods would fall, and so would the oath, taken by the ministers at their solemn ordinations, by which they bound themselves to defend those innovations, and so on. When the votes were taken, all answered unanimously that the oath did not bind them. It is certain that the ministers whom the pseudo-bishops forced into that oath had assumed a fact that does not in truth hold: namely, that the Church had committed to the bishops the power of binding into such an oath those admitted to the ministry, and that those innovations had been introduced by the authority of lawful synods, and that they would not have sworn had they not believed this to be so. But now, since it is plain that the oath was extorted by the bishops through malicious deceit, and they never had this power granted by the Churches, and since it is plain that these synods are illegitimate, the synod declared that those oaths are void and are not to be kept. It also declared that it has always been lawful for presbyteries and provincial synods to exercise all acts of ecclesiastical jurisdiction, especially in the admission and deposition of ministers, since this power has been taken from them by no lawful synod and cannot be curtailed by one.

units.la: Dein examinata fuit causa D. Roberti Hammiltonij, pastoris Glassordensis ; quem causæ suæ procuratorem statuerant Episcopi : Objectum ei præter synodi declinationem, quod ecclesia sæpius deserta, quatuor aut quinque mensibus apud aulam regiam in Anglia hæsisset, quod diem Dominicum publice & ordinarie profanasset, quod juramentis tanquam flosculis ordinarii sermonis usus fuerit, quod alios auditorum suorū sententia excommunicationis violentia summa persecutus fuisset, aliis negaverit obstinatius matrimonium, & quorundum liberis baptismum ; quia genuflexionem in S. cœna non probabant : & cæt. Quæ cum liquido probata essent, functione ministerii indignum declarat Synodus.
units.tr: Next, the case of Mr Robert Hamilton, minister of Glassford, was examined; the bishops had appointed him as the procurator of their cause. Besides his refusal to acknowledge the synod, the charges against him were these: that he had often deserted his church and stayed for four or five months at the royal court in England; that he had publicly and habitually profaned the Lord's day; that he used oaths as the flourishes of ordinary speech; that he had pursued some of his hearers with excommunication with great violence; that he had stubbornly refused marriage to others and baptism to the children of some, because they did not approve of kneeling at the Lord's Supper; and so on. When these charges were clearly proved, the synod declared him unworthy of the ministerial function.

units.la: Sess. 14. Decemb. 6. Die Iovis.
units.tr: Session 14. 6 December. Thursday.

units.la: Quibus commissum fuit libros Canonum, liturgiæ, Ordinationis diligentius excutere, suscepti muneris rationem synodo reddunt, singulorumque animadversiones præleguntur : ex omnibus unam tantum subjungam quæ sic se habuit.
units.tr: Those who had been charged with examining more carefully the books of the canons, the liturgy and the ordination rite gave the synod an account of the task they had undertaken, and the remarks of each were read out. Of all of them I will add only one, which ran as follows.

units.la: Animadversiones in librum liturgiæ ab Episcopis ob- trusum ecclesiæ Scoticæ.
units.tr: Remarks on the book of liturgy obtruded by the bishops upon the Scottish Church.

units.la: Rejiciendus est hic liber. 1. quia obtruditur sine ullo prævio ecclesiæ hujus consensu & approbatione in synodo nationali, penes quam proprie hujus generis negotia definiuntur. 2. quia legitimam & longo usu receptam cultus divini externam formam prorsus abolet, ac in ejus locum substituit aliam a Pontificiis mutuatam, ac ex Missali, Rituali, Breviario Romano desumptam, quæ plurima superflua & ridicula ac superstitiosa continet, semina etiam gravissimorum errorum ac Idololatriæ, ac in multis Anglica liturgia deterior est.
units.tr: This book must be rejected. (1) Because it is obtruded without any prior consent and approval of this Church in a national synod, to which matters of this kind properly belong for decision. (2) Because it utterly abolishes the lawful external form of divine worship, long received by use, and in its place substitutes another, borrowed from the Papists and taken from the Roman Missal, Ritual and Breviary, which contains very many superfluous, ridiculous and superstitious things, the seeds also of the gravest errors and of idolatry; and in many respects the English liturgy is inferior to it.

units.la: Inter alia ridicula ac superstitiosa quæ à Pontificiis mutuatur, hæc sunt. Nam 1. Presbyteri tenentur matutinas & vespertinas illas preces singulis diebus publice vel privatim prælegere, pag. libri illius. 7. Porro si privatim & solus prælegat, quis usus refponfionum per populum: nisi forte intelligendum sit, debere presbyterum sibi respondere nomine ecclesiæ quam repræsentat, & sic preces hæ cum sint publica authoritate institutæ, & prolatæ à publica persona, deputata ab ecclesia ad orandum nomine suo, & hac intentione ut expleat munus suum, quid aliud erunt quam preces illæ Papistarum publicæ, seu horæ Canonicæ, quarum duæ ex septem reponuntur. vide Bellarm. tom. 4. Controvers. lib. 1. De bonis operibus in particulari. cap. 10. 2. Nullus certus locus destinatur matutinis & vespertinis precibus publicis; sed remittitur arbitrio Episcopi, qui sedulo studebit templorum formam ad tempora præcedentia revocare, hoc est, quando Papismus regnabat, ad similitudinem fcil. templi Salomonis, divisi in porticum, navim, & sacrarium. 3. Quædam alta voce à presbytero proferenda sunt, alia vero voce submissa, quæ forma pontificiis consueta est in mysterio Missæ, preces etiam quædam, confessio fidei, & alia jubentur legi aut cani, cum tamen in metrum non redigantur. 4. licet situs corporis indifferens sit, in quibusdam tamen precibus indicitur, ut genibus flexis precemur; in aliis ut stemus; in aliis vero nullus omnino corporis situs imperatur; Et aliquando populus jubetur orare non presbyter, & vice versa, aliquando populus jubetur comprecari cum presbytero, quandoque repetit, quandoque respondet, & alias orationem inter se dividunt, jubetur presbyter aliquando faciem ad populum convertere, aliquando ergo avertit: stare cum legitur Evangelium, sedere cum praelegitur epistola, genuflectere cum Decalogus: Quam frequentem oportet esse libri revolutionem à Psalmis ad collectas, ab iis ad hymnos, inde ad Psalmos, ad lectiones, ad Litaniam. §. Exotica prorsus phraseologia Papismum redolet; etenim plurimas habet voces Scotis penitus barbaras à Romanis factis omnes mutuatas: v. g. Manutinas, vespertinas, Adventum, Epiphaniam, septuagesimam, sexagesimam, quinquagesimam, Dominicam, rogationes, loci ordinarium, collectas, litanias, Venite, Te Deum, Benedictum, Magnificat, Nunc dimittis, sabbatum cantate, Dies cinerum, oblationes, antiphonias, puerperarum purificatio. Actorum Apostolicorum & Prophetarum veteris testamenti capita quaedam dicuntur Epistolae, offertorium, Annunciatio Domine nostrae, officiare, corporale, utraque species, & cæt. Insolitæ &c exoticæ hæ voces, quibus perstringuntur populi aures, metus haud injusti ansam præbet, ne sublatinorum illorum verborum involucro lateantur etiam Sacra Latina. 6. In Calendario, sanctorum numero asscribuntur quidam, cum, an atri fuerint an albi, ignoretur: v. g. Lucianus, Rex David, Kentigernus, Fabianus, Agneta, Vincentius, Blasius, Valertinus, Colmannus, Patricius Episcopus, Cuthbertus, Benedictus, Gilbertus, Serfius, S. Georgius, Dunstanus, Suithinus, Nomen Iesu. Æ-gidius, Ninianus, Adamannus, Sapientia, Crispinus, Hugo Episcopus, Sylvester & cæt. 7. Consessio peccatorum & absolutio ante orationem prælegi jubetur. pag. 35. quasi vero confessio non esset precatio, & in ea, multa à Deo non peterentur. 8. Verba illa conclusoria orationis Dominicæ, quia tuum est regnum, & cæt. aliquando omitti jubentur, aliquando recitari; & cui bono? 9. Singulis diebus, Te Deum laudamus, prælegi aut cani jubetur, quasi hymnus ille ab hominibus compositus, Psalmis omnibus à spiritu S. dictatis sanctior esset. 10. Presbyter, clerici, & populus alta voce simul omnes repetant orationem Dominicam. pag. 42. quam hoc confusum, & annon presbyteri sunt ex clero? 11. In litania, complurima nomina & titulos Deo ascribunt, & multoties unam eandemque orationem repetunt, octies libera nos Domine, vicies & bis Te rogamus audi nos, presbyter designat solum mala, quae populus orando deprecatur; bona itidem, quae populus orando petit. 12. Per mysterium sanctae incarnationis, nativitatis, circumcisionis, baptismi, jejunii & tentationis tuae, per agonem & sanguineum sudorem, per crucem & passionem, per pretiosam mortem & sepulturam, per gloriosam resurrectionem & ascensionem tuam in caelum libera nos domine; quid hoc est aliud quam mera adjuratio? 13. Post 44. orationes, inter quas una est oratio Dominica, dicunt, precemur, quasi praecedentia omnia in orationum censu non veniant. 14. Observandum quod in lectionibus S. coenae destinatis, epistola ponatur ante Euangelium, quod est contra ordinem Biblicum; & quod gratiae non referantur Deo post lectionem epistolae, cum tamen sollicite cautum fit ut Euangelii lectionem clauderet semper doxologia. 15. Dicitur, innocentes illos, infantes ab Herode crudeliter necatos, testes fuisse Christi, seu martyres, et Dei laudes expressisse non loquendo sed moriendo. Ubi varia fe ipsa produnt, tum quod infantes illi sine ulla explicatione dicantur Innocentes, quod Pelagianismum redolet. Et quod omnes in genere testes seu martyres Christi dicantur, cum tamen nec habitu nec actu martyres dici possint: non habitu, seu animi resolutione, multo minus actu, cum nec pro fide quam ignorarunt, nec in fide omnes mortui vere & firmiter dici possint. 16. In collectis tertiae & quartae dominicae post Epiphaniam, & in septuagesima sima praelegitur deprecatio quorundam periculorum quasi dies illi magis fatales essent aliis: 17. In collecta tertiae dominicae Quadragesimae petitur tutela contra hostes; quasi dies illi huic periculo magis subjiceretur aliis, aut quasi preces illo die praelectae ad malum illud praecavendum sufficerent. 18. dies passionis tres habet collectas, cum alii unam, alii vero nullam prorsus habeant. 19. In collecta duodecimae dominicae post trinitatem, petitur, ut ea lagiri velit Deus, quae precibus rogare non audent: an haec est Christianorum ἀλνεοφοβία[?]? 20. Notandum, omnes fere collectas de verbo in verbum translatas esse ex Missali Romano. 21. In rubrica S. coenae praefixa, Sacra mensa instrui iubetur tapete, et mundo panno lineo, et aliis decoris utensilibus, in quorum numero quin veniant superstitiosa illa omnia quibus altaria sua ornant Papistae, vid. crux, candelae, phylacteria, substratoria, quid impediet? praesertim cum haec sibi displicere nullibi ostenderint libri hujus architecti. 22. Iubetur Presbyter officiaturus stare ad septentrionalem altaris partem seu latus, quem vestitu missatico indui oportebit si ita Episcopis visum fuerit: nam anno 1633. nihil ad summam diligentiam reliqui fecerunt, ut Regi serenissimo concederetur facultas, quem vellet pastoribus habitum in sacris imperare. 23. Post repetitam orationem Dominicam iubetur presbyter facie ad populum conversa clare & distincte recitare Decalogum; & populus jubetur se interea in genua provolvere; unde satis innuitur aversa a populo facie recitandam esse a presbytero orationem Dominicam, & submissa etiam voce; quaerendum porro cur populo genuflectendum sit dum praelegitur Decalogus, & idem situs corporis non urgeatur dum precatio Dominica recitatur. 24. Ecclesiae oeconomo vel Diacono mandatur, ut pelvim cum fidelis populi oblationibus summa cum [?]reventia presbytero officianti offerat, qui eandem submissa genuflexione altari imponet, ac Domino offeret. Ubi later.
units.tr: Among the other ridiculous and superstitious things borrowed from the Papists are these. (1) The ministers are bound to read aloud those morning and evening prayers, in public or in private, every day, p. 7 of that book. Further, if he reads them privately and alone, what is the use of the responses by the people? Unless perhaps it is to be understood that the minister must answer for himself in the name of the Church he represents; and so, if these prayers are established by public authority and uttered by a public person, appointed by the Church to pray in its name and with the intention that he discharge his office, what else will they be but the public prayers of the Papists, or the canonical hours, of which two out of seven are retained? See Bellarmine, vol. 4, Controversies, book 1, On Good Works in Particular, chap. 10. (2) No fixed place is assigned to the public morning and evening prayers, but it is left to the discretion of the bishop, who will diligently strive to restore the form of churches to earlier times, that is, to the time when Popery reigned, after the likeness of the temple of Solomon, divided into porch, nave and sanctuary. (3) Some things are to be uttered by the minister in a loud voice, others in a low voice, a practice customary with the Papists in the mystery of the Mass; certain prayers too, a confession of faith and other things are ordered to be read or sung, although they are not reduced to metre. (4) Although the posture of the body is indifferent, yet for some prayers kneeling is prescribed, for others standing, and for others no posture of the body at all is commanded. Sometimes the people are ordered to pray and not the minister, and vice versa; sometimes the people are ordered to join in prayer with the minister, sometimes they repeat, sometimes they respond, and otherwise they divide the prayer between them. The minister is at one time ordered to turn his face to the people, at another to turn away; to stand while the Gospel is read, to sit while the epistle is read aloud, to kneel while the Decalogue is read. How frequently the book must be turned over, from the Psalms to the collects, from these to the hymns, then back to the Psalms, to the lessons, to the Litany! (5) The entirely exotic phraseology smacks of Popery; indeed it has very many words quite barbarous to the Scots, all borrowed from the Romans: for example, morning and evening prayers, Advent, Epiphany, Septuagesima, Sexagesima, Quinquagesima, Dominica, rogations, the usual place, collects, litanies, Venite, Te Deum, Benedictus, Magnificat, Nunc dimittis, Sabbath cantate, Ash Wednesday, oblations, antiphons, the purification of women after childbirth. Certain chapters of the Acts of the Apostles and of the Prophets of the Old Testament are called Epistles, offertory, Annunciation of our Lord, officiate, corporal, both kinds, and so on. These unusual and exotic words, which assault the ears of the people, give no unjust cause for fear that under the covering of those Latin words even Latin sacred things may lie hidden. (6) In the Calendar, certain persons are counted among the saints, though it is unknown whether they were black or white: for example, Lucian, King David, Kentigern, Fabian, Agnes, Vincent, Blaise, Valentine, Colman, Patrick the Bishop, Cuthbert, Benedict, Gilbert, Serf, St George, Dunstan, Swithin, the Name of Jesus, Giles, Ninian, Adamnan, Wisdom, Crispin, Hugh the Bishop, Sylvester, and so on. (7) The confession of sins and the absolution are ordered to be read before the prayer, p. 35, as if confession were not itself a prayer, and as if in it many things were not asked of God. (8) The concluding words of the Lord's Prayer, for thine is the kingdom, and so on, are sometimes ordered to be omitted, sometimes to be recited; and to what good? (9) Every day the Te Deum laudamus is ordered to be read or sung, as if that hymn, composed by men, were holier than all the Psalms dictated by the Holy Spirit. (10) The minister, the clergy and the people all together repeat the Lord's Prayer aloud, p. 42. How confused this is! Are not the ministers part of the clergy? (11) In the litany they ascribe very many names and titles to God, and repeat one and the same prayer many times: "from all evil, good Lord, deliver us" eight times, "we beseech thee to hear us" twenty-two times. The minister designates only the evils which the people pray to be delivered from, and likewise the goods which the people pray for. (12) "By the mystery of thy holy incarnation, nativity, circumcision, baptism, fasting and temptation, by thy agony and bloody sweat, by thy cross and passion, by thy precious death and burial, by thy glorious resurrection and ascension into heaven, good Lord, deliver us": what is this but mere adjuration? (13) After 44 prayers, among which is the Lord's Prayer, they say "Let us pray," as if all that precedes did not count as prayers. (14) It is to be noted that in the lessons appointed for the Lord's Supper the epistle is placed before the Gospel, which is contrary to the biblical order; and that thanks are not given to God after the reading of the epistle, although it is carefully provided that the reading of the Gospel always be closed by a doxology. (15) It is said that those innocents, the infants cruelly slain by Herod, were witnesses of Christ, or martyrs, and expressed the praises of God not by speaking but by dying. Here various faults betray themselves: first, that those infants are called "Innocents" without any qualification, which smacks of Pelagianism; and second, that they are called witnesses or martyrs of Christ in general, although they can be called martyrs neither in disposition nor in act: not in disposition, that is, in a resolute mind, much less in act, since they did not die for a faith they did not know, and not all who die can truly and firmly be called martyrs in faith. (16) In the collects of the third and fourth Sundays after Epiphany, and in Septuagesima, a prayer is read for deliverance from certain dangers, as if those days were more fatal than others. (17) In the collect for the third Sunday of Lent, protection against enemies is sought, as if that day were more exposed to this danger than others, or as if the prayers read on that day were sufficient to guard against that evil. (18) The day of the passion has three collects, while others have one, and some have none at all. (19) In the collect for the twelfth Sunday after Trinity, it is asked "that God would give those things which we dare not ask in prayer": is this the timidity of Christians? (20) It is to be noted that almost all the collects are translated word for word from the Roman Missal. (21) In the rubric prefixed to the Lord's Supper, it is ordered that "the holy table be furnished with a carpet and a clean linen cloth and other decent utensils." Who will prevent those superstitious things, with which the Papists adorn their altars, such as the cross, candles, phylacteries and altar-cloths, from being included in that number, especially since the architects of this book nowhere show that they dislike them? (22) It is ordered that "the minister about to officiate stand at the north part or side of the altar, and he shall be obliged to put on the Mass vestment if the bishops so think fit." For in the year 1633 they left nothing undone in their utmost diligence, so that the most serene King might be granted the power to command the ministers what garb to wear in sacred things. (23) After the Lord's Prayer is repeated, the minister is ordered, turning his face to the people, to recite the Decalogue clearly and distinctly, and the people are ordered meanwhile to fall on their knees. From this it is sufficiently implied that the Lord's Prayer is to be recited by the minister with his face turned away from the people, and also in a low voice. It is further to be asked why the people must kneel while the Decalogue is read, and the same posture of the body is not urged while the Lord's Prayer is recited. (24) The church steward or deacon is commanded "to offer the basin with the offerings of the faithful people with the greatest reverence" to the minister officiating, who, with the same lowered kneeling, places it upon the altar and offers it to the Lord. Where he lays it...

units.la: 1. Iudaismus, dum Deus praesens supponitur magis in altari ante consecratam eucharistiam, quam alibi, quod commentum nequeunt vel ipsi Pontificii deglutire: 2. Papismus, tum dum populi oblatio praecedit sacrificium, tum dum duae oblationes statuuntur, altera pecuniae, altera panis & vini. 25. Saepius imperatur genuflexio, cum nullibi tamen reperiatur mandatum praeparationis feriae ante communionem, & spiritualis ac interni cultus in ipso actu. 26. Permittitur uti pane illo azymo rotundo, hostias nummularias vocant alii. 27. Iubetur presbyter pro rege orans stare, duae item ponuntur orationes pro rege, nulla pro regina & regiis liberis. 28. Festos dies septimanae subsequentis inter celebrandam coenam significet presbyter. 29. Si infrequentius aut negligentius ad communionem accesserit populus, inter ipsa coenae Sacra ad communionem eundem hortari jubetur presbyter: Porro cum eum certiorem fecerit populus de accessu suo, uti in alia rubrica tenentur, quo fine adhibetur haec adhortatio? quod si nomina sua communicaturi non designarint, neque iis statutum fuisset communicare, nisi forte per eam adhortationem animi propositum mutaverint, an statim admittet presbyter, etiamsi de scandalis ecclesiae non satisfecerint? & si tunc admittantur, an licebit censuram ullam illius scandali nomine postea illis infligere? 30. Quidam dies sacri proprias praefationes habent, quidam non, & quare? 31. Mandatur presbytero officianti stare, non genuflectere, cum orationem consecrationis recitat: & in eo loco consistere quo facilius & majori cum decoro utraque manu uti possit, cum interim solus ad altare stet. pagina 207. Quaerendum merito, quid illud sibi velit; ut utraque manu uti, vel utramque exercere possit? an ut imagines crucis in aere formet? an ut patinam & calicem in altum elevet? & an non diserte rubrica hac statutum sit, ut ad occidentalem altaris partem consistat, facie à populo aversa & ad orientem conversa? Delira-menta & nugae hae theatricae sacrosanctam Domini coenam in comoediam transmutant,& Dei cultum infidelium ludibrio ac piorum dolori exponunt. 32. In oratione consecratoria, verba institutionis per modum orationis ad Deum diriguntur, non ad populum prout constituit Christus. 33. Licet liturgia coenae ab oratione Dominica inceperit, nunc tamen post oblatum Christum. pag.209.repetitur, praemissa notabili hac clausula, Audemus dicere, qua innuitur absque confidentia prius prolatam fuisse, quia scil. nondum oblatus fuit Christus; nugae merae papales. 34. Jubetur presbyter pecuniam oblatam dividere, & semissem sibi sumere, ut esca scil. hac facilius capiatur & hamum opertum deglutiat. 35. Dicitur expedire ut lingua Anglica celebretur baptismus, & cur idem non notatur in reliquis cultus divini partibus? & annon alicubi in regno Scotiae magis expediat sacra omnia celebrare lingua Hibernica, quae sola multis cognita est? 36. Dicitur veteres baptismum administrasse tantum in Paschate & Pentecoste, & consuetudinem hanc imitandam nobis esse quam prope fieri possit, licet in solidum revocanda non sit.pag.215. Quaerendum cur hic facta mentio vetustae illius consuetudinis; an ut ostendatur patres non judicasse baptismum simpliciter esse necessarium? quod libri hujus authoribus in mentem venire non potest, quandoquidem satis diserte postea affirment baptismi necessitatem: An vero ut patres illi accusentur desidiae & negligentiae salutis infantium? sed cur quaeso tum monent monent patrum vestigia, quam presse fieri poterit, premenda esse? Turpe est doctori, &c. 37. In celebratione baptismi: pag. 215. Suceptores non vero parentes monentur ut fonti adsint: & miris elogiis fontis illius baptismalis sanctitas celebratur: quæ quæso major efficacia fontis quam pelvis? 38. Licet curato significatum sit infantem esse Baptizandum, rogare tamen debet, an hactenus baptizatus fuerit.
units.tr: 1. Judaism, in that God is supposed to be present at the altar before the eucharist is consecrated more than elsewhere, a fiction the Papists themselves cannot swallow. 2. Papism, both in that the people's offering comes before the sacrifice, and in that two offerings are set up, one of money and one of bread and wine. 25. Genuflection is commanded more often, yet nowhere is there any order to prepare for a holy day before communion, or for spiritual and inward worship in the act itself. 26. It is permitted to use that round unleavened bread, which others call "coin-wafers." 27. The minister is ordered to stand while praying for the king. Two prayers are likewise appointed for the king, but none for the queen or the royal children. 28. The minister is to announce the feast days of the following week during the celebration of the supper. 29. If the people come to communion too infrequently or carelessly, the minister is ordered to exhort them to communicate even during the holy supper itself. Moreover, when the people have told him of their coming, as they are bound to do under another rubric, for what purpose is this exhortation used? And if those who are to communicate have not given their names, and it had not been settled that they should communicate, unless perhaps by that exhortation they have changed their purpose, will the minister admit them at once, even though they have not made satisfaction for the scandals of the church? And if they are then admitted, will it be lawful afterwards to impose any censure on them for that scandal? 30. Some holy days have their own proper prefaces, some do not. Why? 31. The minister officiating is ordered to stand, not to kneel, when he recites the prayer of consecration, and to take up a position where he can use both hands more easily and with greater decorum, while he alone stands at the altar. (p. 207.) It must rightly be asked what this means: that he may be able to use both hands, or to work with both at once? Is it so that he may form signs of the cross in the air? Or so that he may raise the paten and chalice on high? And has this rubric not plainly enacted that he stand at the western side of the altar, with his face turned away from the people and toward the east? These follies and theatrical trifles turn the most holy Supper of the Lord into a comedy, and expose the worship of God to the mockery of unbelievers and the grief of the godly. 32. In the consecratory prayer, the words of institution are directed to God by way of prayer, not to the people as Christ ordained. 33. Although the liturgy of the supper began with the Lord's Prayer, it is now repeated after Christ has been offered, with this notable clause placed before it, We dare to say, by which it is implied that the prayer was previously said without confidence, because, namely, Christ had not yet been offered. Mere papal trifles. (p. 209.) 34. The minister is ordered to divide the money offered and to take half for himself, so that this bait may be taken more easily and the hidden hook swallowed. 35. It is said to be expedient that baptism be celebrated in English. Why is the same not noted for the remaining parts of divine worship? And is it not somewhere in the kingdom of Scotland more expedient to celebrate all sacred rites in the Irish language, which alone is known to many? 36. It is said that the ancients administered baptism only at Easter and Pentecost, and that we ought to imitate this custom as closely as possible, although it need not be restored entirely. (p. 215.) It must be asked why mention is made here of that ancient custom. Is it to show that the Fathers did not judge baptism to be simply necessary? That cannot come into the minds of the authors of this book, since they afterwards affirm the necessity of baptism quite plainly. Or is it to accuse those Fathers of negligence and carelessness about the salvation of infants? But then why, I ask, do they warn that the footsteps of the Fathers must be pressed as closely as possible? "It is a disgrace for a teacher," etc. 37. In the celebration of baptism (p. 215.), the sponsors, not the parents, are admonished to be present at the font, and the holiness of the baptismal font is celebrated with wondrous eulogies. What, I ask, is the greater efficacy of the font compared with a basin? 38. Although it has been made known to the curate that the infant is to be baptized, he ought nevertheless to ask whether it has been baptized until now.

units.la: 39. Fontis baptismalis peculiaris instituitur consecratio & singulis mensibus mutanda est bis aqua, & consecranda. pag. 216. 40. Ad imitationem veterum, qui adultioribus baptizandis interrogata quædam proposuerunt ante baptismum, vid: An credis? an renuncias diabolo & omnibus operibus ejus, ac inani pompæ mundanæ? an baptizari vis? &c. Eadem interrogata infantibus hic satis ridicule proponuntur; quorum vice respondere jubentur fusceptores; Ego credo firmiter, volo baptizari, &c.
units.tr: 39. A special consecration of the baptismal font is instituted, and the water must be changed and consecrated again twice every month. (p. 216.) 40. In imitation of the ancients, who put certain questions to adults before baptism, namely: Do you believe? Do you renounce the devil and all his works, and the empty pomp of the world? Do you wish to be baptized? etc. The same questions are here proposed to infants, quite ridiculously; in their place the sponsors are ordered to answer: "I firmly believe; I wish to be baptized," etc.

units.la: 41. Suceptores, non vero parentes, tenentur infantem in fide instituere.
units.tr: 41. Sponsors, not parents, are bound to instruct the infant in the faith.

units.la: 42. Dicitur duo in baptizandis requisita esse, pœnitentiam & fidem; quæ præstant infantes per suceptores & sponsores suos: an hæc satis sana? Nam cum baptizentur infantes, quia in fœdere sunt, quo Dominus promisit se fore Deum parentibus & semini eorum, & infantes non sint suceptorum seu patrimorum semen & liberi, quomodo poterit suceptorum illorum fides & pœnitentia infantibus illis prodesse?
units.tr: 42. It is said that two things are required in those to be baptized, repentance and faith, which infants supply through their sponsors and guarantors. Is this sound? For since infants are baptized because they are in the covenant, in which the Lord promised that he would be God to parents and to their seed, and infants are not the seed and children of their sponsors or godparents, how can the faith and repentance of those sponsors benefit those infants?

units.la: 43. In liturgia matrimonii. pag. 242. In peragendis matrimonii sacris, sponsus annulum habet, quem sponsæ non tradet, priusquam presbyteri libro imponatur: hoc scilicet supplet vicem pontificiæ benedictionis per aquam lustralem: Annulum hunc presbyter tradit sponso, qui digitum annularem seu medicinalem sinistræ manus sponsæ eo exornabit, dicens. Ego te hoc annulo spondeo, & corpore meo colo, vel adoro, vel honoro, nam verbum illud quo utuntur, I Worphippe, in sacris adorare vel colere significat. 45. In ordine visitationis infirmorum, pag.249. una & eadem oratio praescribitur in omnium aegrorum usum, eadem exhortationes & consolationes absque ulla variatione. 46. In liturgia sepulturae praelegitur, precatur, canitur. 47. Puerperarum purificatio Iudaismum redolet, & caet.
units.tr: 43. In the liturgy of marriage (p. 242.): in performing the rites of marriage, the bridegroom holds a ring, which he will not give to the bride until it has been laid on the minister's book. This plainly takes the place of the papal blessing by holy water. The minister hands this ring to the bridegroom, who adorns with it the ring finger, or "medicinal" finger, of the bride's left hand, saying: "With this ring I wed thee, and with my body I worship, or adore, or honour thee." For the word they use, "I worship," in sacred language signifies to adore or to venerate. 45. In the order for the visitation of the sick (p. 249.), one and the same prayer is prescribed for the use of all the sick, with the same exhortations and consolations, without any variation. 46. In the liturgy of burial there is reading, praying and singing. 47. The purification of women after childbirth smells of Judaism, etc.

units.la: Inter femina errorum quae dispersa latent, sunt.
units.tr: Among the errors which lie scattered and hidden throughout are these.

units.la: 1. Quod libri apocryphi, veteris testamenti partes dicantur. pag. 11. & quod libri quidam ac capita Canonicae scripturae dicantur minus conferre ad aedificationem, & melius omitti posse quam Apocryphorum capita, quae praelegi mandantur; Plurimum etiam Canonicae scripturae nunquam publice praelegitur, ut Canticum Canticorum & universa Apocalypsis, duobus tantum capitibus exceptis, & parte capitis decimononi: An non ortus inde error Pontificiorum, quo Apocryphi libri statuuntur esse Canonici, ex eo quod in ecclesia legerentur? 2. Observatio festorum sanctis dicatorum, pag. 31. & Angelis: Imo plures statuunt dies sanctos quam Dominus in lege veteri determinavit Iudaeis: An non hinc successit sanctorum cultus religiosus apud Pontificios? 3. Devicta mortis acerbitate, aperuisti regnum coelorum omnibus credentibus, pag. 38. & in epistola praelegenda ad vesperam Paschatis, applicatur 1. Pet. 3. 17. Annon sapiunt haec limbum patriarcharum? 4. In ordine sepulturae, pag. 262. orant, ut nos una cum fratre demortuo & aliis omnibus in vera fide & confessione nominis tui vita defunctis, consequamur perfectam absolutionem, & consummata corporis & animae benedictione fruamur. Nonne hinc facile pullulabit precatio pro mortuis? 5. A scortatione & omnibus mortalibus peccatis libera nos Domine. Diserta hic est distinctio peccatorum in mortalia & venialia. 6. Recurrente nativitatis Christi festo, orantes dicunt; hodie natus est Dei filius: unde sequitur, toties natum fuisse Christum, quoties anni à nativitate numerantur, hoc est, 1637. Aut si per diem illum intelligant, mensis non anni diem, oratio illa non erit ex fide, nam ex quo sacræ Scripturæ fundamento colligi poterit illo mense natum fuisse Christum? Idem etiam de circumcisione, Epiphania, & aliis festis. 7. In collecta tertiæ Dominicæ post pascha, dicitur, Deum omnibus in errore versantibus veritatis suæ lucem monstrare, quod adversatur. Psal. 147.19,20. Indicat verba sua Iacobo, statuta sua Israeli, Non fecit ita ulli genti, ideoque jura ista non noverunt. 8. In collecta ad festum S. Michaelis, Michael ille Angelorum princeps, Apocalyps. 12. 7. refertur inter Angelos creatos, cum tamen sit Iesus Christus. 9. In rubrica ante communionem, præparatio in eo sita [?] esse videtur, ut communicaturi vespera præcedente nomina sua presbytero significent, aut eo ipso mane quando administratur S. cœna: licet tum impossibile sit Pastori de vita & moribus communicaturorum inquisitionem instituere, aut tam subito scandala & controversias ac rixas componere. 10. Eadem rubrica, flagrantis scandali reus admittitur ad S. cœnam, modo apud se statuat & profiteatur, se postea satisfacturum, annon Christi instituto directe hoc adversatur, jubentis, prius conveniendum esse fratrem læsum, & illi reconciliandum esse? 11. Sicuti liber hic omni prorsus authoritate ecclesiastica destituitur, sic pag. 29. jubet homilias publica authoritate componendas recipere: unde sequitur, verbi prædicationem & preces à publica illa authoritate civili in universum dependere, & in omnibus religionis negotiis ecclesiam hanc ad cæcam obedientiam astringi, ac fundamentum fidei esse edictum ab aula procuratum, aut procurandum. 12. Oratio offertorii contradicit titulo præfixo : qui sic se habet; Oremus pro universa Christi ecclesia, hic in terris militante: In oratione vero est commemoratio mortuorum, & restrictio Nomenclaturæ Sanctorum ad eos qui gloria nunc fruuntur. Atque sic via sternitur sanctorum Canonizationi & invocationi. Adde quod ibidem preces fiant pro mortuis qui vitæ suæ cursum in fide transegerunt, & nunc à laboribus suis quiescunt, quomodo optime describi animas in purgatorio, fatetur Bellarminus. 13. Auricularis confessio obtruditur conscientiis populi; pag. 204. & absolutio diserte offertur. 14. Modo tres aut quatuor adsint, celebrari poterit communio; pag. 214. qui fortasse erūt, diaconus, subdiaconus & clericus, licet nullus ex populo adfuerit, quid quæso magis refert privatam pontificiorum missam, 15. Ibidem imperatur, ut omnes ter accedant ad communionem annuatim, præsertim vero in Paschate. Iudaicum hoc est, neque legitur Christum alligasse sacramentum hoc cuivis speciali tempori, sed dixit, hoc facite quoties ederitis &c. cæt. 16. Ut persuadeant populo necessitatem baptismi, pag. 216. citant verba illa Christi; nisi quis renatus fuerit ex aqua & spiritu, &c. cæt. quæ tamen de baptismo aquæ non intelligenda sunt, & ibidem dicitur, Deum sanctificasse fontem, prorsus sine ullo scripturæ testimonio. 17. In exhortatione post confignationem crucis in baptismo, fundamentum hoc ut indubitatum ponitur, Omnes baptizatos esse regeneratos. & pag. 224. Infantes baptizatos omnia habere quæ ad salutem necessaria sunt; Quod eorum est axioma qui totalem & finalem vere sanctorum Apostasiam tuentur. 18. Interrogata ad privati baptismi examinationem proposita, pag. 223. præsupsupponunt eos baptizare posse, qui tum formam tum materiam baptismi prorsus ignorant. 19. Dicitur pag. 231. Christum redemisse me & totum genus humanum, quæ phrasis cum nullibi per totum librum commoda aliqua explicatione leniatur, universali redemptioni tam reproborum quam electorum viam præstruit. 20. Dicitur pag.235. duo esse sacramenta in genere necessaria ad salutem: quo innuitur alia esse licet minus necessaria, & in horum numero postea ostendetur collocari ordinem, matrimonium, pœnitentiam & confirmationem. 21. Internæ partes sacramenti S. cœnæ dicuntur, pag. 236. esse, Corpus & sanguis Christi, quæ vere sumuntur in S. cœna, neque ullibi seu in liturgia eucharistiæ, seu in Catechismo, ulla vocula extat, qua phrasis hæc explicetur, aut à commento transubstantiationis distinguatur. 22. Confirmatio, pag. 237. 238. secundum definitionem sacramenti in Catechismo inserto propositam, erit sacramentum; videl. externum & visibile signum internæ & spiritualis gratiæ in nos collatæ, institutum à Christo ut medium quo gratia recipitur, & arrha qua de eadem gratia certi reddamur. Atque hic est signum externum & visibile, manuum impositio per Episcopum, qui solus confirmare potest: Gratia interna & spiritualis, est defensio & vires contra omnes insultus Diaboli, peccati, & mundi, & in precatiuncula post impositas manus dicit Episcopus; Supplices tibi preces fundimus pro hus [?] pueris, super quos ad exemplum Apostolorum tuorum manus imposuimus, ut certiores eos hoc signo redderemus tuæ in ipsos benignæ voluntatis: unde sequitur, Impositionem manuum Episcopi esse signum obsignatorium & medium per quod gratia confertur. Adde quod ratione ministri, qui est solus Episcopus, duobus Genuinis sacramentis præferatur, & sæpius necessaria dicitur hæc confirmatio: quid hæc à pontificiis differunt? 23. Matrimonium etiam tacite inter sacramenta numerari quid vetet? nam annulus contactu libri presbyteri sanctificatus sacrum erit gratiae symbolum, significans, vivendum esse matrimonio conjunctis in mutuo amore & pace, & juxta praecepta Christi. 24. In celebratione matrimonii: pag. 242. Sponsus à presbytero instruitur dicere sponsae: Bonorum omnium meorum te participem facio, seu omnibus meis fortunae bonis te amplifico, In nomine Patris, Filii, & Spiritus Sancti, quibus verbis tenetur maritus bona omnia sua mobilia & immobilia sponsae communicare, nisi perjurus esse velit, ac sacro sancto Dei nomine abuti. 25. In ordine visitationis infirmorum, pag. 253. ægrotus jubetur coram presbytero particularem peccatorum confessionem edere, à quibus à presbytero absolvetur; quam hoc inclinat ad auricularem confessionem. 26. Grassante peste aut quovis alio morbo contagioso permittitur minus S. cœnam cum solo ægroto celebrare, & si cum uno ægro, cur non cum uno quovis alio? 27. Dicitur, pag. 267. In primitiva ecclesia piam fuisse disciplinam, ut initio quadragesimae manifesti peccatores ad publicam pœnitentiam cogerentur, eosque humiliter se submisisse ad subeundam in hoc mundo pœnam, qua eorum animae salvae fierent in die Domini: in cujus locum, donec eadem disciplina restitui posset (quod maxime optandum est) visum est ut hoc tempore coram vobis legerentur generales maledictionis Dei sententiae adversus impœnitentes peccatores: quid hoc aliud est, quam optare ut opera pœnalia satisfactionum restituerentur? & falsum est ullam talem fuisse in primitiva ecclesia consuetudinem, nisi forte corruptam ecclesiam Romanam eo elogio cohonestare velis. Nonne vel hoc satis indicabit, authores hujus libri ad ecclesiam præsentem Romanam inclinare?
units.tr: 1. That the apocryphal books are called parts of the Old Testament (p. 11), and that some books and chapters of canonical Scripture are said to contribute less to edification, and that they may be better omitted than the chapters of the Apocrypha, which are ordered to be read aloud beforehand. Moreover, most of canonical Scripture is never read publicly, such as the Song of Songs and the whole of Revelation, except for two chapters and part of the nineteenth chapter. Did not the error of the Papists arise from this, by which the Apocryphal books are held to be canonical because they were read in the Church? 2. The observance of feasts dedicated to the saints (p. 31) and to the angels. Indeed, they establish more holy days than the Lord determined for the Jews in the law of Moses. Did not the religious cult of the saints among the Papists follow from this? 3. "Having overcome the bitterness of death, you have opened the kingdom of heaven to all who believe" (p. 38). And in the epistle to be read beforehand on the evening of Easter, it is applied to 1 Pet. 3.17. Do not these things smell of the limbo of the patriarchs? 4. In the order of burial (p. 262) they pray that we, together with our brother who has died and all others who have ended their lives in true faith and confession of your name, may obtain perfect absolution and enjoy the full blessing of body and soul. Will not prayer for the dead easily spring up from this? 5. "Deliver us, O Lord, from fornication and all deadly sins." Here is a clear distinction of sins into mortal and venial. 6. When the feast of Christ's nativity returns, they say in prayer: "Today the Son of God is born." From this it follows that Christ has been born as many times as years are counted from his birth, that is, 1637. Or if they understand by that day the day of the month and not of the year, that prayer will not be from faith, for from what foundation of Holy Scripture can it be gathered that Christ was born in that month? The same also holds for the circumcision, the Epiphany and other feasts. 7. In the collect for the third Sunday after Easter, it is said that God shows the light of his truth to all who are in error, which is contrary to Psalm 147.19, 20: "He declares his word to Jacob, his statutes to Israel.
